articleTitle: Challenges and opportunities for Metrology
abstract: Summary form only given. The world of metrology is changing quickly and now extends far beyond its traditional activities in physics and engineering. This review will touch on and illustrate the major challenges in some of the new areas of activity such as chemistry, laboratory medicine, and biology as well as reflecting on a few of the challenges that are being addressed in the more traditional areas

articleTitle: Femtosecond Laser Frequency Combs for Ultraprecise Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract form only given. During the past five years, femtosecond laser frequency comb synthesizers have firmly established their role as ultraprecise tools for optical frequency metrology. The development of these comb synthesizers will be reviewed, and their present and future role in physics and metrology will be discussed

articleTitle: Results of Foresight project and implications for technology
abstract: Summary form only given. The foresight project `Exploiting the Electromagnetic Spectrum' has reviewed the applications that look most likely to give rise to major innovations (science-to-exploitation) over the next 10-20 years, covering the whole spectrum from RF to X-ray, including TeraHertz, infrared and visible. This talk will describe the results of this study, the applications and technologies considered most promising and will then review the implications for measurement needs and technology

articleTitle: Calibration of a 70 GHz Oscilloscope
abstract: This paper reviews work carried out at the National Physical Laboratory on calibrating the responses of 70 GHz bandwidth sampling-oscilloscopes using ultrafast electrical pulses.

articleTitle: Expanding the Measurement Capability for AC-DC Current Transfer at BEV
abstract: To expand the measurement capability up to 100 A at 100 kHz a construction for current shunts and Tee-connectors has been made, calculated and manufactured up to 40 A until now

articleTitle: Improved Model and Phase-Angle Verification of Current Shunts for AC And Power Measurements
abstract: The phase angle error of the output voltage of resistive shunts may depend on a number of stray impedance components. These components have been estimated for some shunt designs. Their total contribution has been measured by a LCR meter method and compared to a step-up procedure. The agreement between the different methods, for measureme nt of phase angle difference of two shunts, was within a few murad at 1500 Hz

articleTitle: Design of a Calculable Cross-Capacitor
abstract: A new calculable cross capacitor is being constructed at NML as part of a new impedance standard. Imperfections in geometry, close approach nonlinearity, gaps between bars and interferometric length measurement are expected to contribute less than 5 nF/F to the uncertainty of the new standard. A second, identical capacitor is also under construction and will be installed at the BIPM

articleTitle: A Measurement Method for the Antenna Factor of Small Loop Antenna by Measuring the Input Impedance
abstract: A new measurement method for the magnetic antenna factor of a small circular loop antenna is proposed and described. It is possible to obtain the magnetic antenna factor of a small loop antenna from Faraday's law and the input impedance of the antenna. The result shows that the proposed measurement method is effective for loop antennas

articleTitle: Calibration of 1000 V/50 Hz Inductive Voltage Dividers and Ratio Transformers
abstract: The paper presents a system for the calibration of inductive voltage dividers (IVDs) and ratio transformers at voltages up to 1000 V and frequencies from 50 to 1000 Hz. The aim is to achieve an uncertainty of calibration less than 1 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> of input

articleTitle: Japan National Standard of Attenuation in the Frequency Range of 10 MHz to 18 GHz
abstract: An attenuation measurement system employs an IVD at 1 kHz as a reference standard and dual-channel IF substitution method is developed to renew the Japan national standard of attenuation. The new system has a measurable attenuation range of 100 dB at frequencies from 10 MHz to 12 GHz, and besides 60 dB up to 18 GHz

articleTitle: Use of Complex Valued Least-Squares Solver Techniques for Adaptor S-Parameter and 3-Port Source Match Determination
abstract: Least-square solver techniques have been evaluated for use in the accurate determination of the S-parameters of non-insertable 2-port devices and the effective source match of 3-port devices in the frequency range 10 MHz to 50 GHz. The results obtained compare favourably with those made using other methods

articleTitle: Preparation of Quantum Hall Effect Device Arrays
abstract: The preparation of quantum Hall effect device arrays at the PTB using multiterminal connections has been improved by the use of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> as insulation material for the multilayer connections. The used lay-out avoids connections crossing the active sections of the devices. Arrays with ten devices in series as well as in parallel have been realised and successfully tested

articleTitle: Improved Sampling Wattmeter for Low Frequencies (45 HZ-55 HZ)
abstract: We have strongly improved our sampling wattmeter for the measurement of low frequency power in the range of 45 Hz to 55 Hz. By using a more stable generator and by correcting for the dc offset in the signals, the basic accuracy in the phase measurement has been improved with a factor of 100 to the level of 20 mudegrees. This improvement has largely extended the applicability of the set-up. The more accurate phase measurement paves the way to e.g. characterisation of AC resistors, as well as power measurements at higher frequencies

articleTitle: AC Voltage Reference Based on a Capacitive Micromechanical Component
abstract: The design and characterization of a high stability capacitive MEMS device intended for an AC voltage reference at 100 kHz or higher frequencies is presented. Preliminary results from a first prototype device show that the pull-in voltage of the device is stable to within 10 ppm over 60 hours. We discuss an optimised device design which is expected to show greater stability

articleTitle: A Method to Determine the Phase Angle Errors of an Impedance Meter
abstract: A method to determine the phase angle errors of an impedance meter up to 1 MHz is described. The accuracy of the method is demonstrated by using the calibrated impedance meter to measure the inductance of resistive current shunts. The measured inductances of the shunts agree with the expected values within a nanohenry

articleTitle: Impedance Measurement using a Least-Squares Waveform Fitting Algorithm
abstract: A waveform fitting algorithm is used to measure the frequency response of a linear impedance. This method is capable of determining the harmonic amplitudes of a triangular signal up to the 50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic. Amplitudes 80dB below the fundamental can be measured by using a 16-bit analogue to digital converter (ADC)

articleTitle: A Digital System for Calibrating Active/Reactive Power and Energy Meters
abstract: A new digital calibration system for AC power and energy meters was developed at Japan Electric Meters Inspection Corp. (JEMIC) and its performance has been evaluated at National Research Council of Canada (NRC). The results at power frequency were better than 20muW/W of apparent power at any power factor settings

articleTitle: A Simplified Treatment of Uncertainties in Complex Quantities
abstract: Calculation of measurement uncertainty for complex quantities can in the general case be done with covariance matrices and Jacobians. We show analytically how complex uncertainties, with the assumption of circular uncertainty regions in the complex plane and uncorrelated variables, can be treated according to the procedures of GUM just as non-complex uncertainties

articleTitle: Modeling the Wave Propagation Properties of Power Cables using Numerical Simulations
abstract: The high frequency properties of coaxial power cables are modeled using time- and frequency-domain numerical simulations. This is required due to the complex helical structure of the outer metallic screen. It is established that this screen design causes a dependence of the cable characteristics on the surrounding medium

articleTitle: Settling Times of High-Value Standard Resistors
abstract: An investigation of the response of high-value resistance standards and elements to applied potential has shown that the processes used to prepare and construct high-value resistance standards can affect the settling times of these standards. Improvements made to the processes used at NIST to fabricate high-value resistance standards will be discussed

articleTitle: CCEM Key Comparison CCEM.RF-K10.CL (GT/RF 99-2) Power in 50 Ω Coaxial Lines, Frequency: 50 MHz to 26 GHz
abstract: This paper describes the performance and results of the Comité Consultatif d'Électricité et Magnétisme (CCEM) key comparison for RF power in the coaxial 3.5 mm line system up to 26 GHz. The values of the power sensor calibration factor measured by twelve national metrology institutes (NMI) show a good agreement at all seven frequencies.

articleTitle: TE018 Dielectric-Resonator Technique for Precise Measurements of the Complex Permittivity of Lossy Liquids at Frequencies Below 1 GHz*
abstract: We describe a novel cylindrical TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01delta</sub> mode dielectric resonator used to measure the complex permittivity of liquids. We performed measurements at frequencies of 422 MHz and 970 MHz on 1-propanol alcohol, methyl alcohol, deionized water, and conductivity-standard solutions of water and potassium chloride. Rigorous mode-matching analysis was used to determine the complex permittivity. Type B measurement uncertainties were estimated to be less than 0.01 for the relative permittivity and less than 0.01 for the loss tangent

articleTitle: Frequency Uncertainty Analysis for Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: The uncertainty in voltage measurement in a Josephson voltage standard (JVS) is proportional to the uncertainty in frequency measurement. The 10 MHz time-base from various commonly used frequency standards for JVS are analyzed using Allan variance to determine the contribution to the uncertainty budget for voltage measurement. The 75 GHz microwave source along with phase-lock electronics and frequency counter for a Josephson junction array is also analyzed for its stability and contribution to JVS uncertainty budget. The results provide realistic estimation for uncertainty contributions of time base and frequency measurements in JVS

articleTitle: Antenna Pattern Measurement using Photonic Sensor and Near-Field Scanning Techniques
abstract: We have developed the planar and spherical near-field measurement systems using a photonic sensor as the probe and verified that the photonic sensor can be considered as an ideal infinitesimal electric dipole probe in the near-field measurements

articleTitle: Influence of Non-Ideal TRL Calibration Items on VNA S-Parameter Measurements
abstract: For the 7-term TRL calibration of a four-sampler vector network analyser (VNA), expressions are presented for the deviations of the S-parameters of two-port test objects (d.u.ts) as functions of the deviations from the ideal values of the S-parameters of the TRL standards used. The obtained sensitivity coefficients are suitable for the establishment of the uncertainty budget for the S-parameter measurement

articleTitle: Fast resistive attenuators for high accuracy measurements of LI voltages
abstract: Design, construction and calibration of compact, inexpensive and fast resistive attenuators for lightning impulse or surge voltage measurements up to 1.5 kV is presented. Estimated uncertainty of attenuator ratio is less than 100 ppm (k=2). The input resistance of attenuators is 50 Omega plusmn 1 % and the rise-time is less than 1 ns. The calibration procedure of the attenuators is described

articleTitle: Apparatus for Measuring the Cylindricity of Calculable Cross-Capacitor Electrodes
abstract: An apparatus has been developed for the precise measurement of the departure from a true cylinder of a 50 mm diameter bar. Four orthogonally disposed capacitance probes are mounted on a stage which can be moved along the rotating bar. The capacitance measurements use a novel technique employing sigma-delta modulation of the bridge arm voltage

articleTitle: Pulse Drive Electronics for Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesis
abstract: Two sets of dedicated electronics for driving Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizers (JAWS) have been manufactured as part of a European collaboration. Their different architectures are described in detail. The results from the characterisation of their electrical outputs are also presented

articleTitle: Inductance Calibration Method Using a Commercial Lcr Meter
abstract: A simple calibration method, which determines inductance from the capacitance standard using a commercially available LCR meter, is presented. Two 10 mH standard inductors were calibrated against a 1 muF reference capacitor at 1592 Hz. The relative combined standard uncertainty was estimated to be 7.4 muH/H

articleTitle: Improvements in the AC-DC Current Transfer Calibration Capabilities at NRC
abstract: NRC Electrical Standards Group is upgrading its shunt calibration facility to offer calibrations up to 100 A at 100 kHz. Primary standards of ac-dc current transfer difference have been verified using fast reversed dc source. A custom set of coaxial shunts has been built and is being characterized

articleTitle: Calibration of Inductance Standards
abstract: A double-balance bridge and a measurement set-up based on the three-voltmeter method are used to calibrate inductance standards by linking them with reference capacitors or resistors. For inductances from 1 mH to 100 mH and frequencies up to 5 kHz, the calibration uncertainties are less than 1 part in 104.

articleTitle: A New Magnet Design for the METAS Watt Balance
abstract: At the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology and Accreditation (METAS), the watt balance apparatus has undergone important changes in the magnetic circuit. A new magnet design has been carefully studied, experimentally tested and successfully integrated in the existing set-up. The details of this development as well as new alignment capabilities are described

articleTitle: Frequency Dependence of the Dissipation Factor of Capacitors up to 10 KHZ
abstract: The frequency dependence of the dissipation factor for two types of capacitance standards have been determined with the use of a parallel plate capacitor. The absolute measurements of dissipation factor have been performed at 1 kHz, 4 kHz and 10 kHz

articleTitle: A Lumped Array Josephson Pulse Quantizer for Quantum-Based Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizers
abstract: Central to quantum-based arbitrary waveform synthesizers is the Josephson pulse quantizer. Its linear dimensions should be small compared to the line wavelength in order to generate an ac voltage with quantum accuracy. Therefore, we use coplanar strip transmission lines to integrate a large number of Josephson junctions into a short array

articleTitle: Application of DMM Linearity to dc Volt Traceability
abstract: The high linearity and stability of modern top-level digital multimeters (DMM) can be exploited to measure voltage ratios with very low uncertainty by making two separate absolute voltage measurements. We developed an integrated approach to apply commercial multimeters as voltage ratio standards for the dissemination of the volt over a wide range of values, based on a JAVS as primary ratio standard and DMMs as secondary standards. The DMM characterized in linearity can find application in top level calibration laboratories, where it can replace the Kelvin-Varley divider in calibration of meters. Moreover, we developed a GPIB interfaced voltage divider that allows the fully automatic calibration in dc voltage of generators

articleTitle: Biasing Josephson Junctions with Optoelectronically Generated Pulses
abstract: A new way of biasing an array of Josephson junctions using optoelectronically generated pulses is described. This method facilitates the generation of positive and negative electrical pulses needed for bipolar waveform synthesis and provides an easy way of optimising the array bias using variable optical attenuators

articleTitle: Bilateral Comparison Of AC Current Ratio Standards up to 700 HZ Between NMIJ and NRC
abstract: A binary type self calibrateable AC current comparator (CC) was developed at NMIJ. In order to confirm the reliability of the new AC current ratio standard at NMIJ, a bilateral comparison was conducted with NRC using an error compensating current transformer. The paper describes an error estimating procedure for the CC and the results of the bilateral comparison

articleTitle: Calibration of Standard Capacitors of 0.01 - 1 μF at NMIJ/AIST
abstract: To provide calibrations of standard capacitors of 0.01-1 muF, a four terminal-pair bridge has been developed. The combined standard uncertainty in the calibration of the 0.01 muF capacitor based on a quantized Hall resistance was estimated to be 0.54times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>

articleTitle: Fast Josephson Arrays for Voltage and Impedance Metrology
abstract: We introduce an optimized Josephson double array generating two independent voltages up to 1.5V using only one microwave input. Such an array, combined with the quantum Hall resistance, can provide the basic traceability for an electricity metrology laboratory from DC voltage to capacitance. We describe the array and present preliminary experimental results from DC measurements. Extending the output voltage up to 10V is discussed

articleTitle: Numerical computations and measurements on calculable resistance standards based on NiCr thin film
abstract: Coaxial AC resistance standards based on a metallic thin film of NiCr deposited on a short stick of ceramic have been developed at BNM-LNE (Caizergues, 1993). Resistors of 1 kOmega and 10 kOmega nominal values have been constructed. Comparisons with a straight wire resistor of Haddad type allow to evaluate their frequency performances otherwise determined by numerical computations using Flux3D finite elements analysis software

articleTitle: Development of Time Comparison Equipment for ETS-VIII Satellite
abstract: The CRL (Communications Research Laboratory) and the JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) are planning to conduct a precise time and frequency transfer between an atomic clock on the ETS-VIII satellite and a ground-reference clock. The CRL is developing special equipment for this precise time transfer link. That conducts the two-way time transfer using the carrier phase measurement method. We expect to obtain a precise measurement exceeding 10 ps between the on-board standards and ground reference clocks. The development of the time comparison equipment, which underwent electrical tests, was finished. We are constructing the ground stations and planning detailed experiments

articleTitle: A Method for the Dissemination of the AC-Voltage of a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: A method to accurately measure ac-voltage in the presence of common mode based on guarding is presented. This allows the dissemination of the fundamental accuracy of a Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS) at high output voltage levels using terminated arrays. A measurement set-up for the comparison of JAWS with a thermal transfer standard with amplified mV-ranges is described

articleTitle: Magnetic Circuit Design for the BNM Watt Balance Experiment
abstract: BNM has started since 2001 the development of a watt balance experiment. The authors present in this paper the design of the magnetic circuit intended to equip it

articleTitle: Discrepancies Between the DC and AC Measurement of Low Frequency Electrical Conductivity
abstract: The measurement of electrical conductivity of non-ferrous metals and alloys is of particular interest to the coin production and handling industries and to the aerospace industry as it provides a measure of the quality of parts. These industries use commercial conductivity meters which measure the parameter using an AC technique. Traceability to national standards in many countries is achieved using DC measurement techniques, although the UK's National Physical Laboratory (NPL) has an established method for achieving this traceability by an AC technique. Due to the effects of frequency and the behaviour of the materials used as reference standards, discrepancies can exist between the AC and DC techniques. This paper describes work undertaken during a project, called Conductivity, aimed at addressing these discrepancies recently completed by a consortium of partners and funded by the European Commission's Framework 5 Programme on Competitive and Sustainable Growth. The partners are 3 national metrology institutes (NPL (UK),' PTB (Germany), NMi (Netherlands)), 2 European instrument manufacturers in this area (Hocking NDT Ltd (UK), Institut Dr Foerster (Germany)) and a representative of the aerospace industry (EADS launch vehicles)

articleTitle: Generation of Constant Voltage Steps by a Josephson Array Driven by Optoelectronically Generated Pulses at BNM-LNE
abstract: Here we report the first results obtained at BNM-LNE on a Josephson array biased by optoelectronically generated pulse trains over repetition frequencies, f, from 0.5 to 1.75 MHz. For all the frequencies, we have observed quantized voltage steps as a function of the current pulse amplitude I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>. We demonstrate the independence of the step widths with f in close agreement with the numerical simulations and we confirm the flatness of a single voltage step

articleTitle: Characterization of a High-Resolution Analog-to-Digital Converter with an Ac Josephson Voltage Source
abstract: An alternating current (ac) Josephson voltage source (Williams, et. al., 2002) was employed to characterize the dynamic behavior of a high-resolution 28-bit (8 frac12-digit) integrating analog-to-digital converter (ADC) of a digital sampling voltmeter (DSV), which is widely used in ac metrology at the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt - PTB. Extensive measurements were carried out to validate previous mathematical models of the DSV (Ramm, et. al., 1999) when sampling ac signals. Some measurement methods and results thereof are presented

articleTitle: Quartz Planar Multijunction Thermal Converter as a New AC-DC Current Transfer Standard up to 1 MHz
abstract: The new generation of PMJTCs on quartz membranes and on quartz crystal chips developed at the PTB results in new ac-dc current transfer standards for the current of 10 mA and the frequency range from 10 kHz to 1 MHz, accompanied with small uncertainties. For a PMJTC with a heater resistance of 240 Omega the uncertainties for frequencies up to 100 kHz are smaller than 1 muA/A and up to 1 MHz they increase to 5 muA/A (k=1). A model for the PMJTC has been developed which allows calculating the ac-dc current transfer difference as well as the attributed uncertainties. The agreement of the simulation and the measurement were tested for high heater resistances of 700 Omega and 240 Omega, for which quite large ac-dc differences are calculated. The good agreement validates the model

articleTitle: An Environment Stabilized Super High Resistance and Its Measurement
abstract: The development of DC high resistance standards from 10 MOmega to 100 TOmega and a dual-voltage-sources bridge is described. The resistance standards are significantly less sensitive to humidity and temperature variations as they are mechanically sealed in a thermostat chamber. A method, for calibrating 10 MOmega to 100 TOmega resistors, is described with results and uncertainty budgets reported

articleTitle: Flat-Spot Measurements for an Ac Josephson Voltage Standard
abstract: Recent advances in circuit design and fabrication of superconducting integrated circuits have enabled us to demonstrate for the first time an ac Josephson voltage standard (ACJVS) that generates both ac and dc waveforms up to 242 mV peak voltage. Using a FFT (fast Fourier transform) spectrum analyzer and an ac/dc transfer standard, we characterize ACJVS operating margins by performing "flat-spot" measurements at the level of a part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> for all eight bias parameters

articleTitle: A Precise Active Voltage Divider for Power Measurements
abstract: In the field of power measurements, a precise, measurable copy of the test quantity "voltage" must be generated which can then be fed to the multiplying device properly. An inductive divider allows this copy of the voltage to be obtained at power frequencies (50 Hz) with a long-time stability and measurement uncertainty of approx. 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6 </sup> in the divider ratio according to magnitude and phase. It is also possible to use a resistive divider. In the following it will be shown, how a broad-band, unloaded phase-accurate resistive divider can be set up by means of amplifying techniques as well as guarding and shielding techniques respectively

articleTitle: The Study of Both Two-and Three-Dimensional Models of Magnetic Shielding Effectiveness for Comparators
abstract: A new numerical method used to calculate the magnetic shielding effectiveness for comparators is given. The both two- and three-dimensional models of magnetic shielding effectiveness of heavy current comparators are established and the results are given for the first time. The experiment shows that the results are quite ideal

articleTitle: Johnson Noise Thermometry using a Quantum Voltage Noise Source for Calibration
abstract: We describe our progress towards a high-precision measurement of temperature using Johnson noise. Using a quantized voltage noise source (QVNS) based on the Josephson effect as a calibrated noise source, we have been able to measure the gallium and water triple point temperatures with an accuracy approaching 100 ppm

articleTitle: High Temperature Coaxial Line Measurement Cell using Room Temperature Calibration
abstract: This paper describes another use of the coaxial line technique for the measurement of the permittivity and permeability of magnetic and dielectric materials at elevated temperatures. The proposed modified coaxial measurement cell allows making fast and accurate broadband measurements taking advantage of a single room-temperature calibration. Measurements are performed from 50 MHz up to 20 GHz. The new coaxial cell is experimentally validated. Results for glass and ferrite samples, in the 20-300 degC temperature range, are presented

articleTitle: Synthesis of Precision Ac Waveforms using a SINIS Josephson Junction Array
abstract: A synthesizer of precision AC waveforms based on a binary SINIS Josephson junction array has been developed. The array segments are individually biased using a high-speed bias source with a 250 ns switching time between voltage steps. The accuracy limitations of the system will be discussed and various measurements between the synthesizer and thermal converters presented

articleTitle: Study for a 43Ca+ Optical Frequency Standard
abstract: The authors proceed with a research and development of an optical frequency standard based on the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> - <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 </sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> transition of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</sup>Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> in a RF trap. For this purpose, motional sidebands of a single <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</sup>Ca <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ion were observed and a stable laser-diode system for spectroscopy of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">43</sup>Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> are being developed

articleTitle: Realisation of a Quantum Standard for AC Voltage: Overview of a European Research Project
abstract: The European JAWS project addresses the lack of instrumentation and knowledge for accurate and traceable measurement and generation of altemating (AC) voltage with arbitrary waveforms. The objective is to develop a standard based on a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS), a precise instrument that links the generated voltage to the Josephson effect, which in turn relates the voltage to fundamental constants and a frequency. The standard aims at synthesized voltages up to 10 mV, frequencies up to 10 kHz and uncertainty smaller than 1 part in 104. This paper reports on the progress in developing tie key components for JAWS.

articleTitle: BNM-SYRTE fountains: Recent results
abstract: This paper describes several recent improvements of the BNM-SYRTE fountain ensemble. A new method for controlling the cold collision shift with improved accuracy has been proposed and demonstrated. A thorough investigation of some cold collision properties of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">133</sup>Cs is presented, including the observation of molecular Feshbach resonances. Finally, a new microwave synthesis scheme based on a fully operational cryogenic oscillator is presented. With this, a fractional frequency instability below 2 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-14</sup>tau<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-frac12</sup> is obtained routinely

articleTitle: Development of a Quantum AC Voltage Standard Based on Externally Shunted Josephson Arrays
abstract: An AC-voltage standard operating at 1 V level at 1 kHz based on nonhysteretic Josephson junction arrays (JJA) is under development. The electronics connected to the array is now sufficiently fast and noiseless when aiming at a 1-ppm accuracy. Some preliminary results and the current setup and status are reported

articleTitle: Calibration System for Electronic Instrument Transformers with Digital Output
abstract: A high accuracy system for calibration of electronic instrument transformers with digital output is described. Its design is based on IEC standards 61850, 60044-8, 60044-7. The calibration system has been built and its performance evaluated. Its estimated amplitude uncertainty is within 50middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> and its estimated phase uncertainty within 50 murad

articleTitle: Wide-Range Optical Attenuation Standard by Incremental Attenuation Method
abstract: We have developed a system for measuring the linearity of fiber-optic power meters over a dynamic range of about 100 dB based on the incremental attenuation method. An example of measurement results is presented, and uncertainty factors are discussed

articleTitle: High-Performance Thin-Film Multijunction Thermal Converter Developed at AIST
abstract: For wide spread distribution of multijunction thermal converters (MJTCs), thin film MJTCs with a novel structure have been developed. In order to reduce the effect of thermal ripples to the output voltage for MJTCs, the authors introduced an AlN chip under a Cu electrode on which Bi/Sb thermocouples are integrated. The thermoelectric transfer difference of the new MJTCs was evaluated to be less than 0.2 muV/V and their ac-dc differences was measured to be less than 10 muV/V in the frequency range from 10 Hz up to 1 MHz. The maximum output EMF for developed MJTCs was 35 mV

articleTitle: Accurate Frequency Atlas of 1.5 μm Band of Acetylene Measured by a Mode-Locked Fiber Laser
abstract: We have been developing optical frequency standards based on absorption lines of acetylene molecules. Using optical frequency comb generators such as a mode-locked fiber laser, we are now measuring difference frequencies between each rotational-vibrational transition and a P(16) line of acetylene molecule. These transitions can be used as accurate frequency references for the calibration at telecom region

articleTitle: Development of a Capacitive Mems RF Power Sensor Without Dissipative Losses: Towards a New Philosophy of RF Power Sensing
abstract: The development of a novel radio frequency (RF) power sensor is presented based on capacitive micro electromechanical system (MEMS) technology, in which the signal is barely disturbed during the power measurement. Results of the first prototypes and improvements for the second generation of RF power sensors are given

articleTitle: Impact of Sensing Area on the Precision of DC Current Measurement using Magnetic Sensor Arrays
abstract: Magnetic sensor arrays are proposed to measure the electric current in a non-contact way. In order to achieve higher accuracy, signal processing techniques for magnetic sensor arrays are utilized. As these algorithms don't take into account the measurement errors caused by the size of the sensing area in the magnetic sensor, further analysis and discussion are necessary to improve the precision of electrical measurement using magnetic sensor array. This paper presents a method to estimate the impact of the sensing area and the error deduction algorithm of magnetic sensor arrays

articleTitle: A Calculable Dipole Antenna to Cover the Frequency Range 850 MHz to 2.2 GHz
abstract: This paper describes the development of a calculable standard dipole antenna for the frequency range 850 MHz to 2.2 GHz. The performance of the antenna has been evaluated on the open area test site and also in a fully anechoic room. The uncertainty for the antenna factor is better than plusmn 0.3 dB over this frequency range

articleTitle: DC Resistive Divider for 10 V HTS Voltage Calibrator
abstract: Resistive divider for a HTS voltage calibrator (Klushin, 2003) with an output voltage up to 10 V was investigated. The developed self-calibration method and parameters of the main parts of the divider showed, that a combined uncertainty of the voltage ratios in the range from 20 mV up to 10 V does not exceed a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>

articleTitle: Accuracy of an Atomic Microwave Power Standard
abstract: We have studied the accuracy of the atomic microwave power standard. The atoms are cooled and kept in a magneto-optical trap (MOT), then dropped through a terminated transmission line (a rectangular, R-70 type, waveguide). The measurement of the internal atomic state allows an accurate determination of the transmitted microwave power

articleTitle: Exploration of Breast Tumors Utilizing Noninvasive Near-Field Microwave Imaging
abstract: A novel microwave nondestructive testing technique is presented for breast cancer detection. A method utilizing the reflection coefficient at the aperture of a waveguide sensor radiating into a breast is described resulting in theoretical microwave images that clearly indicate the presence of a tumor. These images demonstrate the feasibility of detecting breast tumors using this approach

articleTitle: Improvement on Shielding of a Cryogenic Current Comparator Bridge for Operation in an Unscreened Environment
abstract: This paper presents the investigation and improvement of an automated cryogenic current comparator resistance bridge's shielding for a stable and accurate operation in an unscreened environment under adverse electromagnetic interference condition

articleTitle: Resistor's Linearity Testing
abstract: We need not only precisely made resistor but also ohmic (linear) one. Three type of resistors such as carbon, metal film and foil, which values are selected close to quantum Hall resistances of 6.4532kOmega and 12.906kOmega, were tested at room temperature by the dual frequency method and the third harmonics measuring method, because QHR would be thought as perfect linear resistances within there current limits

articleTitle: Reference Power Analyzer Based on the Non-Coherent Sampling Method
abstract: The paper presents the results of the development and characterisation of a three-phase reference power analyser ENERGOMONITOR 3.1. The power analyser is primarily designed for the calibration of industrial power analysers and for the most accurate field measurements of electrical power. The instrument is based on a method of calculating the measurement results from the array of sampled data that does not require the synchronisation of sampling and test signal frequencies. The analysis of a mathematical model has shown that theoretical errors in the measurement of basic energy quantities with distorted voltage and current waveforms do not exceed 0.003 % for the least favourable combinations of harmonic amplitudes and phases. The paper gives results of calibration of the power analyser against the standards at VNIIM

articleTitle: Maintenance of Magnetic Flux Density Standards on the Basis of Proton Gyromagnetic Ratio at KRJSS
abstract: The proton gyromagnetic ratio (gamma<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">'</sup> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>) plays a fundamental role in achieving a high accuracy in magnetic measurements. The authors have improved a magnetic field standard using the gamma<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">'</sup> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>p-value and related techniques at the KRISS measurement complex for proton gyromagnetic ratio determination. The standard for measuring dc magnetic flux density is intended to cover the range from 20 muT to 2.5 T, with an uncertainty (k = 2) ranging from 4 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> 6 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> T

articleTitle: Oversampling Delta-Sigma ADC for Metrology Applications
abstract: This paper focuses on the performance of the Delta-Sigma ADC for metrology applications and presents a quantum based Delta-Sigma ADC under development by Metron Designs and the National Physical Laboratory which is suitable for DC and low frequency spectrum analysis, voltage and power measurements

articleTitle: Optimizing the Series Connection of Thermal Converters For AC-DC Current Difference Calibration - Improved Model
abstract: When connecting thermal current converters (TCC) in series for calibration of current ac/dc difference, attention has to be paid to the various current leakages that may occur. The series connection has been modelled and a specially designed "T-piece" constructed. Calculations indicate leakage error less than 210<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in delta at frequencies up to 100 kHz

articleTitle: Calibration Theory and Measurement Method of Four-Terminal-Pair Standard Capacitor Frequency Characteristic
abstract: The calibration theory and measurement of four-terminal-pair (4TP) standard capacitor (STD CAP) frequency characteristic are studied for frequencies up to 13MHz. And frequency characteristic of 4TP air-dielectric standard capacitor 1000pF, 100pF, 10pF, 1pF and measurement uncertainty is provided

articleTitle: Wideband Microwave Power Sensor Based on MEMS Technology
abstract: An optimized transmission-type MEMS RF power sensor is presented. The design is based on microwave filter theory. It is shown that the thermal resolution of the sensor can be reduced below -50 dBm for RF bandwidths up to les 40 GHz

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Impulse Calibrators with a High Resolution Digitizer
abstract: The lightning impulse voltage calibrators, developed at NML and MIKES-HUT, and a recently developed commercial digitiser were compared. With this three-way comparison, not only the accuracies of the devices were compared, but also the linearity of both peak voltage and time parameters of the devices was investigated. The results demonstrated that the linearity of the calibrators is superior to that of the digitiser

articleTitle: Improved AC-Field Calibration-Setup
abstract: In order to increase the number of measuring points at various frequencies, program controlled operation of the existing ac-field calibration setup has been implemented, leading to a further improvement of its capabilities. The frequency range for the calibration of field coils and instruments, providing an uncertainty in the order of 0.1 %, could be extended up to 150 kHz

articleTitle: The BNM watt balance project
abstract: A new watt balance project is now developed by the BNM: the general configuration and the main parts of the experimental set-up in development are presented. Its aim is to contribute to the international effort in monitoring the kilogram towards a new definition of the mass unit. with an accuracy of 10-8 or better.

articleTitle: Modeling Warm-Up Drift in Commercial Harmonic Phase Standards
abstract: We develop an empirical model for the warm-up drift in harmonic phase standards used to calibrate the phase distortion of nonlinear vector network analyzers. This model will enable us to estimate the time at which the standards reach stability

articleTitle: Nordic Comparison of the Calibration of 1Ω and lOkΩ Resistors Euromet.EM-S18
abstract: The Euromet.EM-S18 resistance comparison have been carried out between Danish Fundamental Metrology (DFM), Swedish National Testing and Research Institute (SP), Centre for Metrology and Accreditation in Finland (MIKES) and Justervesenet (JV) from May to November 2003. This was a comparison of the calibration of 1 Ω and 10 kΩ resistors performed with different measurement system. One conventional direct current comparator (DCC) resistance bridge and three cryogenic current comparator (CCC) resistance bridges were used in the comparison. The final results from the comparison will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Analysis of Complex-Valued Quantities in Magnitude and Phase
abstract: In the evaluation of uncertainty related to complex-valued measurements, coverage factors must be derived in order to account for the probability for the measurand to lie within a given uncertainty region, generally of elliptical form (Ridler, 1998). These coverage factors are dependent on the type of two-dimensional probability density function (PDF) assumed. Traditional approaches assume bivariate normal distribution in the real and imaginary components. In this paper a new definition for the PDF is explored, which assumes Gaussian distribution for the magnitude and uniform distribution for the phase. This so-called Gaussian magnitude PDF is compared with the bivariate normal distribution in real and imaginary. For both models, coverage factors for the usual confidence level of 95% are derived

articleTitle: Precise frequency measurements of 6s 2S1/2 -6p 2P3/2 transition in 133Cs atomic beam using a femtosecond laser frequency comb
abstract: Optical frequencies of the hyperfine components of the D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 </sub> line in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">133</sup>Cs are determined using high-resolution spectroscopy and a femtosecond laser frequency comb. The achieved frequency uncertainties are <10 kHz, which is 10 times better than previous results

articleTitle: Building a frequency-stabilized mode-locked femtosecond laser for optical frequency metrology
abstract: We constructed a frequency-stabilized mode-locked femtosecond laser for optical frequency metrology. Results of the frequency measurements of I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-stabilized 633 nm HeNe laser and 532 nm frequency-doubled Nd:YAG laser and a cesium-atom-stabilized 852 nm diode laser are presented in the conference

articleTitle: Normal Mode Offsets in High Performance Digital Multimeters
abstract: The presence of a normal mode ac voltage can generate a significant dc offset in a digital multimeter (DMM). We have measured this offset for a range of instruments and find that it is more pronounced in high performance DMM's. This effect is related to the use of more complex differential amplifiers in the preamplifier stage.

articleTitle: Snap-shot MRI
abstract: Abstract form only given. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) emerged from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) in the early 1970s. It was clear from the first images that a conceptual breakthrough was required to speed up the imaging process from around one hour for those early images to something more acceptable in medical diagnosis. This step forward came in 1975-6 with the realisation that single-shot images could be obtained in principle by exploiting the properties of spin-echoes commonly used in NMR. The thinking was that an echo train contained, in effect, picture information in one-dimension if obtained in the presence of an external magnetic field gradient. The problem was how to encode the data along the orthogonal axes. The simple initial solution was to add a low-level read gradient while the spin-echoes were forming. This procedure did indeed lead to an image but it contained more image artefacts, which needed to be corrected. Subsequent development removed most of the problems so that today we can produce echo-planar images (EPI), which are subsequently free of artefacts and therefore are of diagnostic value

articleTitle: Applying Advanced Techniques for High Resistance Measurements
abstract: This paper describes results in developing advanced techniques for measuring resistances in the range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> ohms. The use of transfer methods with a teraohmmeter is discussed, with detailed analysis of the factors influencing uncertainty

articleTitle: Experimental Method to Determine the Thermal Isolation Line Effect on the Efficiency of the Bolometer Mount in a Microcalorimeter
abstract: A direct experimental method is proposed to obtain the effective efficiency of the bolometer mount. The effect of the thermal isolation line is measured directly in a microcalorimeter set-up with a short-circuited line. The set-up similarities here reduce the uncertainty causes. The results show a better uncertainty comparing to the indirect estimate or modelling methods

articleTitle: Vector Measurements of Passive Intermodulation Products
abstract: Investigations into vector measurements of reflected passive intermodulation (PIM) at 1775MHz have shown that this technique is valid and enables more accurate characterization of the measurement system's PIM and consequently could lead to increased accuracy low level PIM calibrations of RF components for use in base station applications

articleTitle: Narrow Lines in Molecular Iodine at 501.7 NM
abstract: We report here experimental results obtained in saturated absorption spectroscopy of iodine in a low pressure cell at 501.7 nm. We obtained lines of 30 kHz wide (HWHM) for the R(26)62-0 transition, which are, to our knowledge, the narrowest resonances ever observed in iodine spectroscopy in cell

articleTitle: The Approaches of Decreasing Measurement Uncertainty of CCC
abstract: The uncertainty source in measurement with CCC apparatus is discussed. Experiment shows that the uncertainty in operation of CCC is mainly from the pressure fluctuation of helium gas in cryostat. Some approaches of decreasing the uncertainty are proposed. In addition, increasing the turn number of the CCC windings can improve the S/N ratio in measurement and is also effective for decreasing the measurement uncertainty

articleTitle: Analysis of Harmonics in the Power Measurement
abstract: The paper gives an account on a new power measuring system, based on digital sampling, which was developed by the National Institute of Metrology (INMETRO) of Brazil. The goal of the project was to achieve the highest possible accuracy at the presence of considerable harmonic distortions, to guarantee full traceability to national standards and to minimize the costs of obtaining a high quality reference system. The system facilitates the calibration of commercialized electronic wattmeters, watt-hour meters, as well as the analysis of non-linear loads, resulting harmonic distortions in power systems

articleTitle: Recent Improvements in NIST-Fl and Resulting Accuracies of δf/f<7x10-16
abstract: Since our last publication describing the accuracy budget for NIST-FI (a laser-cooled Cs fountain primary frequency standard) the authors have made many improvements resulting in nearly a factor of 2 reduction in the uncertainty in the realization of the SI second. Recently the authors reported a combined standard fractional uncertainty of 0.67times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup>

articleTitle: Measurement of the 88Sr+ reference transition frequency with a new probe laser system
abstract: The authors have designed and implemented a new 674 nm (445 THz) laser system for probing the ultranarrow 5s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>-4d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> reference (clock) transition of the trapped and laser-cooled <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</sup>Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+ </sup> ion. The authors describe briefly the double-stage probe laser system; linewidths of (50 plusmn 9) Hz FWHM were observed for the clock transition with this source. Results on the determination of the temperature of zero thermal expansion coefficient of the reference cavity were also presented. Preliminary measurement of the absolute frequency of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88</sup>Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> clock transition frequency gives a frequency of (444779044095472 plusmn 15) Hz

articleTitle: Accurate Analysis of Smoothly Modulated AC Waveforms Applied to the Calibration of Fluctuating Harmonic Analysers
abstract: Calibrated harmonic analysers are required to underpin international regulations regarding harmonic emissions for electrical appliances. A method to accurately analyse waveforms containing smoothly fluctuating harmonics is described. The response of an analyser to the characterised waveform is considered and a method to calibrate an analyser is presented

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Accurately Estimating the Harmonic Magnitudes of Periodic Arbitrary Signals using Asynchronous Sampling
abstract: An algorithm that uses an integrating voltmeter for accurately estimating the harmonic magnitudes of periodic arbitrary signals is presented. The uncertainties associated with the magnitude estimates relative to the fundamental depend on signal stability, harmonic content, noise variance and are less than 1 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> for signals with up to 64 harmonics

articleTitle: Optical Frequency Measurements using Fs- Comb Generators
abstract: We have used a Ti:Sapphire- based fs-comb generator to measure the frequencies of several optical frequency standards available at PTB

articleTitle: AC Power Bridge at NMIJ
abstract: At NMIJ, an accurate ac power bridge was developed to calibrate power meters at 100 V, 5A, and frequencies from 50 Hz to 120 Hz. This project has been implemented in 2001 due to the master plan of NMIJ

articleTitle: New Multi-Frequency Method for the Determination of the Dissipation Factor of Capacitors and of the Time Constant of Resistors
abstract: A new method for the simultaneous detennination of the dissipation factor of capacitors and of the time constant of resistors by a multi-frequency method is presented. This method is based on the measurement of impedance ratios at two or more frequencies. A bridge is set up with a programmable two-channel ac voltage source and the impedances to be compared. The impedance ratios are determined by synchronous sampling procedures and application of discrete Fourier transform. In a first experiment, a high-grade gas-filled l-nF standard capacitor was compared with a stable 1-MΩ ac resistor at frequencies between 40 Hz and 660 Hz. The estimated standard uncertainties (k = 1) are 0.7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> for the dissipation factor of the capacitor and 0.6 ns for the time constant of the ac resistor.

articleTitle: Traceable Measurement of Magnetic Moment and DC Susceptibility
abstract: A number of traceable force susceptometers have been developed at NPL. A low moment system is available for calibrations performed at NPL, while the Davis susceptometer is more suited to locations without a dedicated magnetics facility. Traceability to national standards has been established for both of these techniques

articleTitle: HTS Superconducting Current Comparator: Dynamic Range and Noise Limits
abstract: The dynamic range and noise have been investigated for our novel High Temperature Superconductor (HTS) dc current comparator in which a current concentrator is used to improve the flux sensitivity. Initial applications for non-invasive sensing of charged-particle beam currents are envisaged. Potential applications of this technique to fundamental metrology, such as in a physical determination of the faraday by an ion-collection method, are also under consideration.

articleTitle: Recent Development of Terahertz Wave Time-Domain Technology
abstract: Terahertz (THz) radiation, which occupies a large portion of the electromagnetic spectrum between the infrared and microwave bands, offers innovative imaging and sensing technologies that can provide information, which is not available through conventional methods (i.e. microwave and X-ray techniques.) Recently, governmental supported THz wave related fundamental research in science and application emphasized technology development has increased substantially. As THz wave (T-ray) technology improves, we believe new T-ray capabilities will impact a range of interdisciplinary fields, including: communications, imaging, medical diagnosis, health monitoring, environmental control, and chemical and biological identification. This is particularly crucial for identifying terrorist threats in homeland security (three to five years), and medical diagnosis or even clinical treatment in biomedical applications (five to ten years)

articleTitle: An Alternatwve Formulation for Uncertainty Analysis with Correlated Estimates
abstract: A formulation for uncertainty analysis with correlated estimates is proposed. Consistency with GUM is demonstrated. This formulation has a feature that the variables appearing in the formula have good match with experimentally measured quantities

articleTitle: Steps Towards a Capacitance Standard Based on Single-Electron Counting at PTB
abstract: A quantum standard for capacitance is realized by charging a capacitor with a well-known number of electrons and measuring the voltage U across the capacitor by means of a Josephson voltage standard (Williams et al., 1992), This experiment yields quantum determination for the capacitance C = Ne/U where N is the number of electrons and e the elementary charge. Currently, PTB is working on the realization of such an experiment using single-electron pumps for transferring electrons one by one to a cryogenic vacuum capacitor. We report on the progress in the development of the different components for this experiment, with emphasis on measurements characterizing the single-electron tunneling (SET) circuit

articleTitle: Investigations on the Electrometric Transfer Standard
abstract: Further investigations have been made on the electrometric ac-dc transfer standard. The measurements by means of this instrument have been indirectly compared to the preliminary results of the international comparison CCEM-K9. The ac-dc transfer differences were also checked for the dependence on the distance between the electrodes and for the long-term drift

articleTitle: A New Configuration for the Maxwell-Wien Bridge
abstract: We report a new configuration for the Maxwell-Wien bridge, with some simple and innovative solutions used in the construction of the bridge developed recently by Inmetro

articleTitle: Diameter determination of Avogadro sphere #1 and #2
abstract: In the scope of the new determination of Avogadro's constant, NA, the spheres interferometer of PTB was developed to measure the volume of the Avogadro sphere. The interferometer is based on spherical reference plates and spherical beams of rays. This allows not only one diameter in the center to be measured, but a big amount of diameter measurements available in a 60deg field of view. With all orientations of this 60deg cone a sphere is characterized by 500 000 diameter values. Avogadro sphere #1 of PTB and Avogadro sphere #2 of IMGC have been measured in 40 different orientations, so that fundamental knowledge of the spheres can be given. The additional information of surface topography leads to better understanding of uncertainty

articleTitle: A Standard Quantum Measuring System for Reproduction and Measurement of Low Direct Magnetic Field in the Range 0.1 μT-1.5 mT
abstract: A wide-range low permanent field standard measurement system is described, intended for use within the geomagnetic range of natural magnetic fields on the Earth's surface (EMF) (20 μT - 100 μT), fields of near and distant outer space (0.1 μT - 20 μT), and precision current-carrying high-uniform-field coil systems used in fundamental and applied research (up to 1.5 mT)

articleTitle: Ratio Transformer and its Calibration
abstract: A ratio transformer has been developed with currents from internal loading being compensated by means of auxiliary adjustable current sources connected in accordance with a proposed "parallel" equivalent circuit. The compensating currents are injected to section taps of the coaxial screen of a ratio winding. The application of a splitted magnetic system eliminates necessity of magnetic shielding of the transformer. The additional section with double shielding and adjustable potential provides self-calibration with uncertainty about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9 </sup>. The results of self-calibration have shown that the errors of the decade voltage ratio do not exceed 20 nV/V (in-phase) and 50 nrad (quadrature) at 1 kHz

articleTitle: A Novel Apparatus for Measuring Permeability of Weak Magnetic Material
abstract: The weak magnetic material is widely used for electrical and electronic devices. To measure the dc permeability of the material more precisely and easily, a novel apparatus is developed. It can be used for the specimen in large plate shape directly and the tedious preparation of special specimen is unnecessary. Therefore, this apparatus may be used for industrial procedure where the dc permeability of the weak material is important

articleTitle: Key Comparison CCEM-K6.c of AC-DC Voltage Transfer Standards at Selected Frequencies between 1 MHz and 100 MHz
abstract: From August 1995 to September 1998, the CCE 92-05 comparison of ac-dc voltage transfer standards at selected frequencies between 1 MHz and 100 MHz was carried out (van Mullem, 1999). From December 1998 until mid 2000, some participants carried out additional measurements and actions to complete the comparison as the key comparison CCEM-K6.c. The results at all frequencies show a good agreement between most of participants

articleTitle: A Hybrid Electronically Coupled Current Comparator
abstract: A versatile electronically coupled current comparator is presented in the paper. With four-decades of its variable turn windings replaced by fixed turn windings, it features a simpler design more convenient for manufacturing yet retaining high accuracy. It provides a resolution of 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> and has an estimated uncertainty in the order of 10middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>

articleTitle: Research in Automatic Measurement System of The EMF Secondary Standard
abstract: In this paper, the research of auto-measurement system of the EMF secondary standard is introduced. The system is composed of the standard cell enclosure, temperature measurement instrument, and low thermo-EMF programmable multi-channel switch. The system can make auto-measurement. The result shows the uncertainty of the system is below 1.7x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8 </sup> (k=l)

articleTitle: Improving the Accuracy of the CA Optical Frequency Standard
abstract: We demonstrate the reduction of residual Doppler shifts for a laser-cooled neutral atom optical frequency standard to near negligible levels through use of second-stage laser cooling and atom interferometry. For the NIST Ca optical clock, this opens up the possibility for uncertainties of less than 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup>

articleTitle: Performance Improving of KRISS Micromachined Multijuntion Thermal Converter
abstract: Thin-film multijunction thermal converters (MJTCs) with chromel-constantan thermocouples and an Evanohm R alloy heater were fabricated using semiconductor process and bulk micromachining. The voltage sensitivity and the ac-dc voltage transfer differences were evaluated. And the ac-dc transfer differences seem to be stabilized below the value of 1 ppm in the frequency range from 1 kHz to 500 kHz

articleTitle: Compact Inductance Standard
abstract: An inductance standard for realization inductance unit with uncertainty about 1 muH/H within a frequency range 0.5-3 kHz has been developed and investigated. Being very compact, the standard can be used for realization of key comparison with a simplified procedure of the traveling standard circulation

articleTitle: Seven-Port Wave-Correlator Based Vector Network Analyzer
abstract: A seven-port wave-correlator based vector network analyzer (VNA) is proposed. The seven-port wave-correlator is a combination of two six-port wave-correlators. The complex wave ratio measurement accuracy, however, is improved since the input signals are directly detected by the side-arm ports. The performance of the developed seven-port wave-correlator and the constructed network analyzer are evaluated, and the measurement accuracy is confirmed

articleTitle: Comparison of Density Difference Measurements by Flotation at PTB and NMIJ
abstract: The results of density difference measurements by the flotation apparatuses of NMLJ and PTB for four silicon samples are reported. The flotation method is used to investigate the inhomogeneity and to determine the absolute density of silicon crystals for the determination of the Avogadro constant

articleTitle: A cold atom interferometer for high precision inertial measurements
abstract: The authors are developing a high precision inertial sensor. This device uses cold Caesium atoms manipulated by stimulated Raman transitions (Berman, 1997). As this setup is sensitive to both acceleration and rotation, two counter-propagating beams of cold atoms are used to discriminate between the two contributions. The last experimental results will be presented here

articleTitle: Coherent Population Trapping for Electromagnetic Field Measurement
abstract: Coherent population trapping resonances at the D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> line of Cs are examined under the influence of constant and alternating magnetic fields. It is shown that electromagnetic fields as low as a few mG modify significantly the shape of the resonances, which can be used for electromagnetic field measurement

articleTitle: CCEM key comparison "Magnetic Flux Density by means of Field Coil Transfer Standard"
abstract: The coil constant k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> - i.e. the quotient of magnetic flux density in the coil centre over the coil current - of a Garrett type field coil has been determined in units as maintained by various standard laboratories. Most of the laboratories have also measured the coil constant k(f) as function of frequency up to f = 20 kHz

articleTitle: Comparison Euromet.EM-K8 of DC Voltage Ratio: Results
abstract: Twenty National Metrology Institutes have participated in the European DC voltage ratio key comparison (EUROMET.EM-K8). The results for the voltage ratios 1000V/10V and 100V/10V are reported

articleTitle: Comparing Different Methods for the Calibration of the mV Ranges of an AC Measurement Standard
abstract: A new method has been developed for the calibration of an AC measurement standard at 20 mV and below using a resistive voltage divider (RVD). Measurements made with the RVD are compared to measurements using the existing "bootstrap" method given in the service manual and also to measurements using an AC/DC transfer standard

articleTitle: Vector Calibration of Optical Reference Receivers using a Frequency-Domain Method
abstract: A frequency-domain integrated-optic modulator based technique to characterise the vector response of an optical receiver is described. The results measured using this new technique are presented and compared with optical impulse and heterodyne measurements.

articleTitle: Towards Accurate Measurement of the Frequency Dependence of Capacitance and Resistance Standards up to 10 MHz
abstract: Progress towards an understanding of the frequency dependence of capacitance and resistance standards at frequencies up to 10 MHz is presented. A qualitative comparison is also made for capacitance and resistance measurements between NPL high-frequency four terminal-pair bridge and a commercial impedance analyzer for the first time

articleTitle: Single Indium Ion optical frequency Standard
abstract: A single indium ion stored in a radio frequency trap and laser-cooled to a temperature below 1 mK can serve as an optical frequency standard of exceptionally high accuracy and stability

articleTitle: The Development of a Digital Sampling System for Low Power Factor Measurements of High Voltage Capacitive/Inductive Reactors
abstract: A digital sampling system for high accuracy low power factor measurements of high voltage capacitive/inductive reactors is described in the paper. It is suitable for automation and since it does not require balancing offers the advantage of faster operation with respect to current comparator based bridges. It has an estimated uncertainty of less than 50middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> under real high-voltage conditions

articleTitle: Turnkey compact frequency standard at 1556 nm based on Rb two-photon transitions
abstract: DiCOS Technologies has developed a high coherence fully automated absolute frequency standard for metrology applications. It uses a 1556 nm narrow linewidth DFB fiber laser locked to a two-photon transition in rubidium 85 at 778 nm after second harmonic generation in a non-linear waveguide crystal. Its main features and performances are presented in this paper

articleTitle: Determination of Frequency Coefficients for Thermal Voltage Converters and Digital Voltmeters by Comparison to Inductive Voltage Dividers
abstract: The Ac-dc transfer project at NIST is expanding the use of inductive voltage dividers (IVDs) for the calibration of high-voltage ranges of thermal voltage converters (TVCs) and digital voltmeters (DVMs). We report on a system to facilitate the comparison of the frequency coefficients between two ranges of TVCs or DVMs to the frequency coefficient of an IVD ratio

articleTitle: Low Voltage Ac-Dc Difference Standards at Spring Singapore
abstract: This paper presents two low voltage ac-dc difference measurement systems established at SPRING Singapore. The systems use micropotentiometers and resistive divider to scale the voltage from primary reference level to 1 mV to provide accurate mV-level ac-dc difference calibration at frequency range from 10 Hz to 1 MHz. The measurement results of the two systems and the loading effect correction are discussed

articleTitle: Determination of G with atom interferometry; status of the experiment MAGIA
abstract: The MAGIA experiment is designed to measure the Newtonian gravitational constant G using atom interferometry. A double differential measurement of the gravitational force produced by heavy source masses on two clouds of atoms allows the determination of G. We present the general idea and actual status of the experiment

articleTitle: CW Doppler-Free Two-Photon Laser Spectroscopy of the 4d105s 2S1/2-4d9 5s2 2D3/2 Transition in Atomic Silver
abstract: We have measured the frequency, isotope shift and hyperfine structure intervals of the 4d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>5s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">frac12 </sub> rarr 4d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> 5s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</sub> two-photon transition in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">107</sup>Ag and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">109</sup>Ag by laser spectroscopy of a thermal atomic beam. Frequencies were linked to the hyperfine component a<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> of the line R111(18-1) in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">127 </sup>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> near 520 THz

articleTitle: Precision Three-Stage 1000 V / 50 Hz Inductive Voltage Divider
abstract: A separately excited three-stage inductive voltage divider (IVD) has been designed for voltages up to 1000 V at frequencies from 50 to 1000 Hz. The IVD provides output to input voltage ratios of 0.001 and 0.01 with amplitude and in-phase uncertainty of the ratio better than 1times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>

articleTitle: 1.5 Micron Acetylene Stabilised Frequency Standard and the Measurement of its Absolute Frequency using an Optical Frequency Comb
abstract: Frequencies of the P(10), P(l 1), P(15), P(16), P(20), and P(21) transitions in the v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> + v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> overtone band of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> were determined using an optical frequency comb generator. The laser frequency showed a stability of 4 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup> in 1 s and a reproducibility of better than 1 kHz

articleTitle: Nano-Scale Squids Application for Single Particle Detection and Spectroscopy
abstract: The advantages gained by a reduction in feature size towards the sub-micrometre or nanometre scale have opened the way to new applications for SQUlDs. We describe our work to employ sub-micron or nanoscale SQUIDs for single particle detection and spectroscopy using a novel inductive superconducting transition edge technique

articleTitle: Traceable RF Peak Power Measurements for Mobile Communications
abstract: A technique is described to provide traceability for RF pulsed power measurements, predominantly used in 2G and GPRS mobile communications. The method is used to verify the performance of an RF pulsed power signal generator and peak power meter

articleTitle: Characterisation of Magnetic Force Microscope Probes for Quantitative Magnetic Field Mapping at Sub-Micron Length Scales
abstract: Magnetic force microscopy is a special mode of atomic force microscopy that can be used to image magnetic features. For the image contrast to be quantitative the tip of the scanning probe needs to be characterised. Methods for achieving this are being developed and the principles behind them are presented here

articleTitle: A Double Calorimeter for 10 W Level Laser Power Measurements
abstract: A new type calorimeter for precise measurement of 10 W level laser power has been designed and fabricated. This is a double configuration consisting of an absorbing unit made of a disk absorber and an isothermal unit. The ratio of the substituted laser power to the dc power is determined for the absorbing unit. The design of basic construction and experimental results are described

articleTitle: Energy Comparison in China
abstract: An energy comparison in industrial frequency of 50Hz has started in China. The metrology institutes of the big regions and of some important provinces participate in the comparison. The comparison purpose and main technical problems are introduced in the paper. The comparison will be finished in June 2004 and the main results would be published in the conference

articleTitle: High accuracy velocity control method directly linked to the speed of light: application to the BNM watt balance project
abstract: We describe a novel method of velocity control that addresses the measurement requirements of the watt balance projects. The method is based on the use of both a heterodyne Michelson's interferometer and a home-made high frequency phase shifting electronic circuit. Results show that intrinsic relative uncertainty of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> on velocity can be reached with this method over a translation range of 80 mm

articleTitle: Progress in the Measurement of the Gravitational Constant using a Cryogenic Torsion Pendulum
abstract: Continuing measurements of G are being made using a cryogenic torsion pendulum in the "dynamic" (time-of-swing) mode. The total metrology contribution to the G error budget is about 7 ppm. Data runs are being conducted using both CuBe and A15056 torsion fibers to test for systematic fiber-dependent effects

articleTitle: Measurement Results with a New Small Cam-Driven Absolute Gravimeter
abstract: We describe the design of and measurement results from a new cam-driven compact and portable absolute gravimeter. The resulting instrument will serve a multitude of field (because of its compactness) and laboratory (including standards) applications

articleTitle: Dynamical Signatures of Competing Nonlinearities Induced Self Phase-Locking in a Triply Resonant Optical Parametric Oscillator
abstract: We report on dynamical signatures of signal/idler self phase-locking in a cw frequency divide-by-three optical parametric oscillator subject to two competing chi<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup> nonlinear processes, confirming the theoretical predictions

articleTitle: Establishment of the National Standards for S-Parameters and Related Quantities in Mexico
abstract: Scattering parameter measurements are very important in fields such as telecommunications. A description of the establishment of the Mexican national standards for providing traceability to these measurements is presented in this work

articleTitle: Traceable Dielectric Measurements of New Liquids for Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) Measurement in the Frequency Range 300 MHz to 6 GHz
abstract: New tissue-equivalent liquids have been developed for specific absorption rate (SAR) measurements in compliance with international standards. They are more physically stable, less toxic and have lower temperature coefficients than existing published liquids. Their dielectric properties have been measured traceably and they have been evaluated in a National SAR-Testing Laboratory (CRL)

articleTitle: Development of Cryogenic Sapphire Oscillator at NMIJ/AIST
abstract: A cryogenic whispering gallery sapphire oscillator has been investigated.
