The prototype sapphire-loaded cavity oscillator was designed to oscillate at 10.812 GHz and exhibited a fractional frequency stability of 6 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-13</sup> at integration times of 1 s, which is limited by a hydrogen maser reference

articleTitle: Precision Spectroscopy of Metastable Atomic Hydrogen: Towards an Improved Determination of the Rydberg Constant
abstract: We describe progress on a new experiment that is underway at NPL to measure the 2S-nS,D transitions in atomic hydrogen using a metastable atomic beam. This work will contribute to an improved value of the Rydberg constant

articleTitle: Intercomparison of Magnetic Flux by Means of Coil Transfer Standard
abstract: EUROMET.EM.M-S1 (Euromet Project no.597) titled "Intercomparison of magnetic flux by means of coil transfer standard" started in the beginning of 2001 with participants from five European countries including CMI (Czech Republic) as the pilot laboratory. The project was successful and finished in 2003

articleTitle: A Microfabricated Spring-Constant Calibration Device for Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) Potentially Traceable to the SI
abstract: We have developed a compact and easy-to-use MEMS (micro electro-mechanical) calibration device for atomic force microscopy, using a method that allows traceability to the SI system. The new device, which we call an electrical nanobalance, is calibrated by a non-contact method, a combination of electrical measurements and Doppler velocimetry. For the AFM user, the device offers a simple, accurate and traceable method for AFM cantilever spring constant calibration, for the first time

articleTitle: Progress on the Quantum Capacitance Standard at Metas
abstract: At the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology and Accreditation (METAS) a quantum primary standard of capacitance based on single electron tunneling devices is under development. In this paper we report on the progress made so far as well as on the current work towards the realization of this standard

articleTitle: Efficient Islolation of fo in an Optical Frequency Synthesizer
abstract: Spliced and connectorized micro-structured fibre, periodically-poled KTP phase-matched for 1064nm SH-generation and a laser line filter at 532nm have lead to an efficient means of extracting the offset-frequency signal from a femtosecond-laser-based optical frequency synthesizer. The optical-to-microwave clockwork has been used to make frequency stability comparisons between optical and microwave radiation sources

articleTitle: Josephson Array Standard Calibrations without Frequency Synchronization
abstract: The standard technique for the calibration of a voltage reference by means of a Josephson array voltage standard (JAVS) is based on the synchronization of the frequency of the microwave irradiated onto the array, typically by means of a phase locked loop. This guarantees a very accurate and stable output voltage from the Josephson array and a quite simple frequency measurement. However, the accuracy level provided by the phase lock method is not required in the calibration of electronic standards, since their intrinsic noise sets the minimum achievable calibration uncertainty several orders of magnitude above the contribution of the frequency uncertainty for a synchronized source. An alternate technique is reported in the following that makes use of the voltage difference between the array and the reference under calibration to control the array frequency. The calibrations performed with the new method agree with the results obtained with the usual one within few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>

articleTitle: Beyond 1 ppb Precision in spl alpha/ from Electron g - 2
abstract: This paper reports the current status of theoretical work on the electron anomalous magnetic moment alpha<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> and its impact on the determination of the fine structure constant alpha. Our aim is to obtain a value of alpha with a precision exceeding 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> when new measurement of alpha<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> becomes available

articleTitle: Design of a KU Band Delay Difference Calibration Device for Twstft Station
abstract: The national metrology institute BNM-SYRTE designed a new Ku band delay difference calibration device for the TWSTFT earth station recently installed at the Observatoire de Paris (Achar and Merck, 2003). It is based on the satellite simulator technique developed by VSL (Jong and Polderman, 1994) and TUG (Kirchner, 1995) with a faster delay calibration process

articleTitle: Determination of Magnetic Moments of Proton and Deuteron
abstract: We consider higher order corrections to the magnetic moment a bound proton in atomic hydrogen and deuterium and their consequences for determination of mu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> and mu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub>. We also report on a measurement with medium-pressure hydrogen deuteride (HD) at 10 atm, which is to be compared with the previous measurement done at 100 atm. We confirm that the high pressure used in former experiments caused no systematic effects at a level of 10 ppb. We also reexamined a theoretical uncertainty related to screening effects in the HD molecule and found that previously it was underestimated

articleTitle: Radiometric Measurements of a Near-Ambient, Variable-Temperature Noise Standard
abstract: A near-ambient, variable-temperature noise standard whose physical temperature can be accurately measured was constructed and then measured with the NIST total-power radiometer to test the accuracy of radiometer measurements in the temperature range of 263 K-325 K over the frequency range 8-12 GHz

articleTitle: Uncertainty Evaluation of a Broadband Attenuation Standard
abstract: We have recently developed a standard step attenuator, composed of 10 steps of build-up chain of power measurement and operating from 10 MHz to 18 GHz. Each step shows a nominal attenuation of about 9 dB and an expanded uncertainty of 0.0018 dB at 30 MHz. The overall system has a dynamic range over 90 dB

articleTitle: Stability-Degradation Factors in an Optical-Microwave Frequency Link System and their Evaluation using Phase Noise Measurement
abstract: We are developing a highly stable optical-microwave frequency link system. We consider the stability-degradation factors in the frequency link system to be the synthesis, the phase lock and the photo detection system of the repetition frequency. We evaluated these factors by undertaking phase noise measurements

articleTitle: Transportable Lowest DC Current Standard
abstract: A new compact transportable lowest current standard for the range from 1 fA to 1 nA was made in VNIIM

articleTitle: Progress in optical frequency measurements at BNM-SYRTE
abstract: We report recent progress in optical frequency measurements at the BNM-SYRTE. The work presented is centered around the development of a frequency measurement chain based on a femtosecond laser (Diddams, 2001) and the construction of an optical frequency standard (OFS) using cold Sr atoms. The Kerr lens mode-locked femtosecond laser is centered at 800 nm with a repetition rate at 840 MHz, locked to a cryogenic oscillator referenced to a primary Cs standard. The frequency comb from the laser is broadened to more than an optical octave in a photonic crystal fiber. The infrared part of the frequency comb is frequency doubled in KTP and heterodyned with the green part of the spectrum to yield the carrier envelope offset frequency. For absolute frequency measurements, the CW laser from an OFS is superimposed with the frequency comb, and the beat signal with an adjacent line is measured. We present recent developments in our setup, as well as recent experiments on high stability transfer between various OFS in the lab

articleTitle: NRC-Metas-PTB Collaboration, Part 1: Bridges for AC QHR Measurements
abstract: The design and evaluation of different bridges used for ac quantized Hall resistance (ac QHR) measurements at NRC, METAS and PTB are presented. These bridges are used to study the frequency, magnetic field intensity, and current dependence of quantized Hall, (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">XY </sub>), longitudinal, (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">XX</sub>), resistances, as well as conventional ac resistors

articleTitle: Allan Variances for DC Voltage Measurements with Polarity Reversals
abstract: Precise measurements of dc voltage were made using a polarity reversal technique and the results were analyzed using the Allan variance. These were then compared with the Allan variances for unreversed or unipolar measurements of the same processes. The Allan variances were found to agree quite well, particularly for sampling times corresponding to the 1/f noise regime for the measurement of Zener-diode voltages

articleTitle: A Precise Measurement of a NbN-Based 1 V Programmble Josephson Voltage Standard Array
abstract: A Josephson voltage standard system with NbN/TiN based SNS Josephson array is under development at AIST. Microwave-induced characteristics of the Josephson array have been precisely investigated

articleTitle: Resistance Ratio Standard with DC-Squid Detector
abstract: Cryogenic current comparators are widely used for resistance scaling. The high accuracy of these comparators is achieved by flux-sensing using a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID). At present commonly RF-SQUIDs are used which are no longer commercially available. First experiments for a replacement with DC-SQUIDs are presented.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two-Way and GPS Carrier-Phase Time Transfer Between CRL and TL
abstract: The data obtained by the two-way satellite time and frequency transfer (TWSTFT) and GPS carrier-phase (GPSCP) experiments between the Communications Research Laboratory (CRL) in Japan and the Telecommunication Laboratories (TL) in Taiwan are compared in this paper. Results with high agreement between the two techniques are described

articleTitle: Measurement Uncertainty Reduction in a Mini TEM Cell
abstract: A method for a mathematical reduction of the dominant uncertainty contribution in a mini TEM cell, caused by reflections in the transition sections, is discussed. A unique measurement method is developed for the validation of the mathematical assumptions

articleTitle: Effects of Device Mounting on AC Quantized Hall Resistance Steps
abstract: Since the previously reported four-port measurements of quantized Hall resistances (QHRs) at the National Measurement Laboratory (NML) some modifications in the device mounting have resulted in changes in the nature of the i = 2 QHR step

articleTitle: A Phase-Locked-Loop Concept for the Generation of Two RF-Signals with a Small Frequency Offset
abstract: A phase locked loop concept for the generation of two extremely stable RF-signals with a small frequency difference is presented based on only one phase locked loop (PLL). The system comprises two crystal oscillators from which one is frequency fixed acting as the reference while the other one is tuneable being controlled by the PLL-system. A special PLL-concept allows achieving a very small frequency difference of only some 100 Hz between the two oscillators while maintaining a short settling time below 2 ms as well as a very good phase-noise performance

articleTitle: Determination of the Quadrupole Frequency Shift of the 2S1/2 - 2D5/2 Transition in 88Sr+ at 674 nm
abstract: In preparation for an absolute frequency measurement referenced directly to the NPL caesium frequency fountain, the authors have made a measurement of the quadrupole shift of the 674 nm transition in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">88 </sup>Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. This allows a determination of the quadrupole moment of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sub> level, which is compared with Cowan code calculations

articleTitle: Quadratic Frequency Dependence of an AC QHR Device
abstract: An equivalent electrical circuit model of an ac quantized Hall resistance device externally connected in quadruple series predicts a quadratic frequency dependence no more than -4 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>/kHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This agrees with experiment when indirectly comparing that device with a calculable quadrifilar resistor in interchanged 1:1 ratios using a four-terminal-pair bridge

articleTitle: Systematical Measurement of Molecular Iodine Hyperfine Transitions in the Wavelength Range of 500-517 Nm
abstract: We report new measurement of the hyperfine spectra of molecular iodine BlarrX transitions in the wavelength range of 500-517 nm. Four effective hyperfine parameters, eqQ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>, d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B </sub>, and delta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> are determined for an extensive number of rovibrational levels in the B state, yielding rich information about the rotational and vibrational dependence of the hyperfine interactions. In particular, abnormal variations in the hyperfine parameters and strong u-g mixing at several levels are observed in this intermediate region

articleTitle: Reducing the Uncertainty in the Measurements of Power and Energy
abstract: A method to minimize the components of uncertainty of a measurement of the quantities of electric power and energy is presented in this work. The measurement procedure is adopted to disseminate the referred units with smaller uncertainties than those inherited due to traceability of secondary standards

articleTitle: Sources of Errors in Measurements of 1.018 v Zener Voltage References and Suggestions for Treating Them
abstract: In Zener voltage measurements, different sources of uncertainty are encountered. Some of them depend on the Zener standard itself, while others depends on the measurement apparatus. We here study some effects that appear when connecting a 1.018V Zener to a measurement apparatus

articleTitle: The Use of Optical Electric Field Sensor to Measure Antenna Radiation Patterns
abstract: An optical electric field sensor combined with a near-field test system was used to determine the antenna radiation patterns. In the measurement system, the sensor head served as a receiving probe and the antenna under test as a transmitting antenna. Measurement results achieved by different methods are presented

articleTitle: South African Frequency Standard Through Digital Diode Laser Stabilisation to a Sub-Doppler Rovibrational Line of Acetylene
abstract: To cater for the needs of industry the CSIR-NML has developed a primary optical frequency standard. The frequency standard is based on a technique of locking a diode laser's output wavelength to an absorption line of acetylene at a known pressure. These absorption lines are a fundamental characteristic of acetylene

articleTitle: Double-Stacked MoSi2-Barrier Junctions for Programmable Josephson Voltage Standards
abstract: We are developing MoSi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-barrier stacked-junction arrays for Josephson voltage standards in order to increase the output voltage, operating bandwidth, and operating margins. In this paper we present measurements of a programmable voltage standard circuit with double-stacked arrays, where two junctions are fabricated in each stack. Although a mask defect prevented operation of one-eighth of the fabricated junctions, the remaining circuit, with a total of 51,344 junctions, succeeded in producing an output of 1.93 V with a range of operating current greater than 1 mA for the combined 13 subarrays

articleTitle: International Comparisons of Transportable Femtosecond Laser Frequency Combs
abstract: Two types of comparisons using transportable femtosecond laser combs have been performed in France and the USA, respectively. The agreement among the combs, when referenced to a hydrogen maser, is on the sub-hertz level at 563 THz. When the combs are referenced to an optical standard, the agreement among four combs was much improved and found to be < 1 mHz at 456 THz

articleTitle: Measurement of the Avogadro Constant and Mise EN Pratique of an Atomic Definition of the Kilogram by A 28Si Single-Crystal
abstract: This paper describes an attempt to replace the present definition of the kilogram with the mass of a certain number of carbon atoms. This requires determination of the Avogadro constant, N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub>, with a relative uncertainty of 1 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>. Silicon crystals are used in this determination. At present, a factor limiting factor is the measurement of the average molar mass of natural Si. Consequently, a worldwide collaboration has been set up, to produce, approximately, 5 kg of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si single-crystal with an enrichment factor greater than 99.985% and of sufficient chemical purity to be used for the determination of N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub> with a target relative measurement uncertainty better than 2 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>. The present article describes the cooperation work-plan, the specifications applied, and quantifies the expected improvement

articleTitle: Improved Capacitance Measurements with Respect to a 1 pf Cross Capacitor from 200 Hz to 2000 Hz
abstract: We describe frequency dependence measurements of fused-silica capacitance standards from 200 Hz to 200 Hz, using a 1 pF cross capacitor as the reference. The relative combined standard uncertainty at 200 Hz (the largest in the frequency range) is 0.11times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6 </sup>, which is smaller by about a factor of two than the uncertainty reported earlier from NIST

articleTitle: Evaluation of NPL CSF1 Primary Frequency Standard
abstract: A full performance evaluation of the caesium fountain primary frequency standard at the NPL is reported. Improved magnetic shielding has resulted in the inhomogeneity of the C-field being below 1 nT. The measurement of the frequency bias due to cold collisions is described. A direct evaluation of the fountain's frequency stability, in comparison to that of a hydrogen maser, is reported

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Single-Ion Optical Frequency Standards at the 1·10-15 Level
abstract: Two optical frequency standards based on the 688 THz (436 nm) transition of trapped <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">171</sup> Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> are compared in order to investigate their instability and systematic offsets. Initial experiments demonstrate a relative Allan standard deviation of sigma <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>(1000s) sime 1middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> and a mean frequency difference of 0.2 Hz at an averaging time of 7000 s

articleTitle: Optical Frequency Standard Based on an Electric Octupole Transition in 171Yb+
abstract: The frequency of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> (F = 0) - <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 </sup>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7/2</sub>(F = 3, m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> = 0) transition in a single, trapped, laser cooled ion of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">171</sup>Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> has been measured with a femtosecond laser frequency comb generator. The uncertainty is limited by measurement statistics and by the AC Stark shift

articleTitle: Measurement of Laser Linewidths and Coherence Lengths using a Frequency Counter
abstract: We describe how the linewidth and coherence length of high purity lasers can be estimated using a frequency counter to replace an optical interferometer of variable length. We also show theoretically and experimentally how such measurements are affected by the finite measurement time

articleTitle: Shielded Electronic Current Transformer
abstract: A current transformer with nominal ratio 10 A to 10 mA, intended for low frequencies applications, was developed. It includes an electronic device to reduce the magnetizing current, and a continuos shield in the secondary winding in order to eliminate the effect of stray capacitances. These lead to high accuracy results (ratio errors and phase-displacements in the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>). It is proposed to leave the cable-shield potential floating.

articleTitle: Optical Collimation of Atomic Beam
abstract: Laser radiation propagating through a hollow-core optical fiber exerts a central force on atoms and transports them through the fiber. This atom guide works as an atomic beam collimator that can continuously control the velocity and spatial distributions of the ejecting atoms via modulation of the laser parameters

articleTitle: Joint IMGC-NMIJ Measurement of the Si (220) Lattice Spacing
abstract: Further details are given of a measurement of the (220) lattice spacing of silicon carried out by jointly the Istituto di Metrologia "G. Colonnetti" and the National Metrology Institute of Japan

articleTitle: Investigations on the uncertainty of FOCS-1
abstract: The uncertainty budget of a primary frequency standard based on a continuous cold cesium beam builds up differently than with a pulsed fountain. This communication reports on a detailed theoretical and experimental analysis of three entries in the continuous case: the collisional shift, the light shift and the Zee-man shift

articleTitle: The Theoretical Analysis of Open-Loop Characteristic for Double Magnetic Detector Comparator
abstract: The open-loop characteristic of the double magnetic detector is calculated in theory based on harmonic balance principle and compared with the testing result. The study shows that the open-loop characteristic of the double magnetic detector has only one operating point corresponding to zero ampere turns, no other zero output points so called false-balance points

articleTitle: Signal/Noise Improvement in Saturation Spectroscopy Enhanced by an Active Optical Cavity
abstract: An original scheme of laser spectrometer based on an active cavity with a saturated absorber has been investigated. A signal-to-noise improvement at an increase of the cavity Q-factor has been demonstrated both theoretically and experimentally. Prospects for applying the active cavity enhanced saturation spectroscopy are discussed

articleTitle: Measurement and Correction of No-Load Losses of Power Transformers
abstract: The paper reviews the practice of correcting the results of no-load loss measurements of large power transformers for the effect of distorted supply voltage waveforms. Data obtained during testing of large power transformers are reproduced and analyzed at the National Research Council laboratory to ensure that the proper corrected losses are determined. The instrumentation requirements for no-load loss measurements, particularly when the transformers under tests are energized line to line are discussed

articleTitle: Using Blind Identification in the Dynamic Characterization of High Voltage Oscilloscope Probes
abstract: The use of a blind identification technique for the characterization of the dynamic performance of oscilloscope and waveform recorder probes used in high voltage measurements is described. The procedure allows the intercomparison of reference systems for calibration at the highest accuracy

articleTitle: The mobile fountain FOM
abstract: The paper presents the improvements of the mobile fountain FOM: an automated laser source has been developed and the cesium tube has been modified. The goal was to increase short term stability and reliability of the clock, in order to gain in resolution for future comparisons

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Accurately Estimating the Phase Shifts Between Harmonics of Two Voltage Signals using Asynchronous Sampling
abstract: An algorithm that uses two integrating voltmeters in a master-slave configuration for accurately estimating the phase shifts between the harmonics of two periodic arbitrary signals is presented. The phase shift between the fundamental components of two periodic arbitrary signals can be measured with an uncertainty of less than 2.5 murad

articleTitle: Solid-State Carrier-Envelope Offset Frequency Detection Via Quantum Interference in Semconductors
abstract: We detect the carrier-envelope offset frequency of ultrashort optical pulses using quantum interference control of injected photocurrents in low-temperature-grown gallium arsenide. With further improvements to the signal fidelity, this solid-state detection method will enable stabilization of the carrier-envelope offset frequency of femtosecond modelocked laser pulses for optical frequency metrology

articleTitle: Zero Baseline and Short Baseline Characterisations of GPS Receivers
abstract: This paper describes the evaluation of a GPS-based remote system for the calibration of precision clocks. Experiments were conducted using multi-channel GPS receivers. Results of zero baseline-common clock and short baseline-common clock common view measurements show that these receivers are suitable for remote calibrations after the correction of delays associated with the measurements

articleTitle: Three-loop radiative-recoil corrections to hyperfine splitting generated by radiative insertions in feriion lines
abstract: We obtain an analytic result for three-loop radiative-recoil corrections to hyperfine splitting in muonium generated by the diagrams with the one-loop radiative photon insertions both in the electron and muon lines. The results obtained here represent the next step in our program of calculating all three-loop corrections to hyperfine splitting in muonium, they improve the theory of hyperfine splitting, and affect the value of the electron-muon mass ratio extracted from experimental data on the muonium hyperfine splitting

articleTitle: Silicon-Based, Tunable-Barrier Single Charge Sources
abstract: We have demonstrated the operation of, and are assessing theoretically and experimentally the error rates of, silicon-based single-electron turnstiles, pumps, and CCDs. These devices are conceptually very similar to the metal-based pumps which have already proven to have a very low error rate; potentially, the Si-based devices have several substantial advantages, including higher current value, higher temperature of operation, and simpler operation

articleTitle: A Test to Measure the Effect of Self-Heating on the Scale Factor of a Measuring System for High Direct Voltage Based on a Resistor Divider
abstract: Unless the temperature of the divider is controlled, the dominant contribution to the uncertainty of resistor dividers used to measure high direct voltage is usually self-heating. This paper presents a simple test which can be used to estimate the change in scale factor caused by self-heating and the uncertainty in this estimate

articleTitle: Progress report of the 133Cs - Fountain Frequency Standard in Brazil
abstract: We present the state of the time and frequency program in development in Brazil. This contribution concerns the last progresses obtained with the atomic fountain (Magalhaes et al., 2004)

articleTitle: Comparison of IMGC and PTB Absolute Determinations of the Si(220) Lattice Spacing
abstract: If we want to base the kilogram definition on the mass of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si atom, the present uncertainty of the Si (220) lattice plane spacing has to be lowered by a factor ten. On the way to achieve this improvement, the comparison between the lattice spacing determinations obtained by combined X-ray and optical interferometry via the Si crystal standards MO*4 and WS5C of the IMGC and the WASO 4.2a one of the PTB is intended to assess the 0.16 part per million shift between the lattice spacing values recently obtained in a joint IMGC-NMIJ measurement and the past values obtained by IMGC and PTB

articleTitle: Compensation of the temperature coefficient of magnetic field coils
abstract: A simple, but very effective method for compensating the temperature coefficient of the coil constant of any magnetic dc field coil to an almost negligible order has been developed. The method is useful for precise single-layer standard coils as well as for multilayer high-field coils

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Frequency Dependence of the Resistance and Capacitance Standards in the BIPM Quadrature Bridge
abstract: The BIPM uses a quadrature bridge to link capacitance standards to resistance standards. The frequency dependence of the resistances used in the quadrature bridge (a pair of 51.6 kOmega resistors) is determined by comparison with a calculable coaxial resistor of 1290.6 Omega. The quadrature bridge can be operated at three different frequencies (1027 Hz, 1541 Hz and 3082 Hz) using three different pairs of capacitors of values 3000 pF, 2000 pF and 1000 pF, respectively. The frequency dependence of each capacitance in this range of frequencies is deduced from these measurements

articleTitle: Development of Multi Channel Dual Mixier Time Difference System
abstract: A multichannel dual mixer time difference (DMTD) system has been developed by the Communication Research Laboratory (CRL) for measurement system to generate UTC(CRL) time scale. This system has a function of measuring time differences between reference signal and 24 DUT signals, simultaneously

articleTitle: Potential of the Single-Frequency CPT Resonances for Magnetic Field Measurement
abstract: Coherent population trapping (CPT) resonances on degenerate two-level system of D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> line of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb were investigated with single frequency laser excitation. Their sensitivity on stray magnetic fields was examined for linear, elliptical and circular laser polarization. Methodology for magnetic field measurement using the CPT resonance is proposed

articleTitle: Investigations of Noise in Measurements of Electronic Voltage Standards
abstract: We have studied the voltage noise of electronic voltage standards based on Zener diode references (Zeners). Ten volt Zener outputs were compared to NIST Josephson standards using a digital voltmeter (DVM) to record voltage differences. The data were analyzed using the Allan variance. We have characterized the 1/f noise of 22 Zeners of three types. We also present evidence for the presence of a high level of white noise in Zeners

articleTitle: Experience with Ac Calibration of Conventional CCC
abstract: Overview of the sources of dc and ac ratio errors in conventional cryogenic current comparator (CCC) is presented. Preliminary results of the measurements of ac ratio error in overlapped-tube type CCC are given. The measured maximum deviation from the nominal ratio in CCC used in MIKES is less than 2 ppm in frequency range 0-200 Hz

articleTitle: Quantum Computation and raising Schrodinger's cat
abstract: Two discrete energy levels in quantum system, such as an atom, can be used to store a bit of information. However, quantum systems can also exist in superposition states, thereby storing both states of the bit simultaneously. This property potentially leads to an exponential increase in memory and processing capacity. It would enable a quantum computer to efficiently solve certain problems, such as factorizing large numbers, which may be intractable on a classical computer. Actually building a useful quantum computer is an extremely daunting task due to the necessity of overcoming decoherence. Nevertheless, in the near term, the principles of quantum information processing may find important applications in metrology. A quantum computer would also realize a mesoscopic version of "Schrodinger's Cat," a bizarre situation where a cat could be simultaneously dead and alive. A number of physical systems are currently considered for building a quantum computer; we focus on examples using atoms, but also discuss other possible implementations

articleTitle: Linkinng and UV Detector Responsivities Via Cavity Enhanced Frequency Doubling
abstract: We demonstrate that a setup for cavity enhanced optical frequency doubling can be used to determine the responsivity of a UV detector at the second harmonic wavelength. This determination relies only on relative power measurements and a known responsivity of an optical detector at the fundamental wavelength

articleTitle: Progresses toward capacitance measurements at ultra-acoustic frequencies
abstract: The Istituto Elettrotecnico Nazionale Galileo Ferraris (IEN) is working to provide capacitance traceability in the ultra-acoustic frequency range (up to 10 MHz). For gas-dielectric capacitors (1-1000 pF), a calibration technique has been developed and the calibration service is now operative. For solid-dielectric capacitors (up to 1 muF), a traceability chain has been identified, and a ratio bridge is under construction

articleTitle: Volume Determination of Silicon Spheres using an Improved Interferometer with Optical Frequency Tuning
abstract: For accurate volume measurements of 1-kg silicon spheres, an interferometer with a direct optical frequency tuning system has been improved. The diameter of a silicon sphere has been measured by the interferometer with a standard uncertainty of 2.3 nm. Details on the improvements and the result of the measurement are described

articleTitle: Probe Influence on the Measurement Accuracy of Non Uniform LF Magnetic Fields
abstract: The error introduced by the coil size averaging effect when measuring non uniform LF magnetic field is analysed with particular reference to the use of field meters equipped with non-concentric coil probes. The analysis is developed by computation and the results are validated by comparison with experimental data

articleTitle: Progress in Development of the Measurement Equipment for the Link Between DC QHR and Capacitance Standards in MIKES
abstract: Results on development of the measurement setup for representation of the farad from DC QHR in MIKES are presented. Measurement chain and designed equipment used in the link between QHR and capacitance are described. Expected uncertainty is parts in 107. The important components of that chain, the standard combining 100 kOhm resistors and 1 nF capacitors and AC 10:1 self-calibrated coaxial resistance bridge, are described in this paper

articleTitle: Bilateral Comparison Kriss-Cenam of 10 pF and 100 pF Standard Capacitors
abstract: This paper describes the recent bilateral comparison of 10 pF and 100 pF fused silica capacitance standards at 1 kHz and 1.592 kHz between KRISS and CENAM. Actions at both institutes were taken with basis on the results of this comparison and the calibration of the used capacitors at BIPM

articleTitle: The IEN CCC Bridge to Scale the Quantized Hall Resistance to 1-Ω Standards
abstract: A cryogenic current comparator bridge, to scale from the quantised Hall resistance to 1 Ω, has been built at IEN. A description is given and preliminary results are reported

articleTitle: Intercomparison of Calibration Systems for Ac Shunts up to Audio Frequencies
abstract: An intercomparison of calibration systems for ac shunt up to audio frequencies between the National Research Council of Canada, Japan Electric Meters Inspection Corporation, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology, U.S.A., is presented. The transfer standard used for the intercomparison is a 10 A, 0.1 shunt

articleTitle: Quantised Acoustic Current Through a Static Quantum Dot
abstract: We studied the influence of a quantum dot in a 1D-channel on the quantised acoustic charge transport. Current plateaux at record-low RF-powers have been observed. More importantly, our findings show a possible way to a systematic engineering of quantum dots for an optimised high accuracy device.

articleTitle: Investigations of AC-DC Transfer Standards in the Near-Infrared Spectral Range
abstract: The purpose of this work was (a) to develop an experimental set-up which is capable to record the time dependent temperature fluctuations of single junction thermal converters due to low-frequency ac currents by using an IR photo detector and (b) a characterisation of the local and temporal temperature behaviour of shunts for the ac current measurements with a thermocamera

articleTitle: Density Measurements for the Avogadro Constant: Discrepancies and Systematic Effects
abstract: Significant discrepancies emerged between the density reference standards of the IMGC and of other NMIs, contrasting with the good agreement of previous comparisons. The reason of these contrasting results lies in a systematic effect linked to the individual pair of standards being compared, due to the balance and to the procedure adopted.

articleTitle: Impedance Bridge Ratio Transformer Calibration by Reference-Step Conductance Build-Up
abstract: A reference-step conductance build-up method suitable for automation has been developed for calibrating the ratio dial transformer of a wide-range impedance bridge. The uncertainties over the range 40 Hz to 20 kHz are estimated not to exceed 0.2 muV/V referred to the divider input voltage. At 100 kHz, the uncertainties do not exceed 2muA7V

articleTitle: Novel Modelling of Magnetic Fields in the BIPM Susceptometer
abstract: Magnetic forces can adversely affect precise weighings. A systematic investigation is aimed at verifying a magnetic susceptometer and its attendant theory by using a numerical model for the magnetic field intensity

articleTitle: APMP International Comparison of AC-DC Transfer Standards at the Lowest Attainable Level of Uncertainty
abstract: The paper presents preliminary results of the APMP.EM-K6a key comparison of ac-dc transfer conducted during 2000-2003. The ac-dc voltage transfer difference of the travelling standard was measured at 3 V and selected frequencies from 1 kHz to 1 MHz that included those of the CCEM-K6a key comparison. Also discussed are the methods used to compare TVCs with different input connectors, and to link the results to the parent CCEM comparison

articleTitle: A Portable Enclosure with High Temperature Homogeneity and Stability
abstract: The development of QHR and CCC technique gives the possibility to establish a resistance standard with uncertainty of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> or less. Thus the requirement of precision enclosure, especially with high homogeneity, becomes essential for practical uses. In this paper the approach to meet this requirement is given. An enclosure with auto-regulated homogeneity has been built. The homogeneity and stability of the enclosure is within 2 mK

articleTitle: Two-photon single mode coupling efficiency: definition, measurement, optimization.
abstract: The authors investigate the physical meaning of coupling a two-photon field (non-classical state of light) into two single mode optical fibers, studying the limits to this due to a non-coherent emission of photons in parametric down conversion, an important starting point for many single photon source schemes

articleTitle: NRC-METAS-PTB Collaboration, Part 2: Linear Frequency Dependence in AC Resistance Measurement
abstract: Several reasons for measuring linear terms in the frequency dependence of ac resistors are presented. They also apply to ac quantum Hall measurements but are just systematic effects of the coaxial bridge and the reference resistor

articleTitle: Improved Optical Frequency Standard with Ultracold Calcium Atoms
abstract: We report on latest improvements in an optical frequency standard based on ultracold calcium atoms. First steps towards a clock using atoms trapped in an optical lattice are presented

articleTitle: An Automated Co-Axial Ac Resistance Bridge
abstract: An automated co-axial ac bridge has been constructed, by substituting automated inductive voltage dividers (autoIVD's) for manual dividers in a standard 4 terminal-pair bridge design. The bridge has been used to measure the ratio of two 100 Omega resistors. A Tinsley 100 Omega ac/dc resistor has been found to change value by 0.1 parts per million (ppm) from 500 Hz to 2500 Hz, with a type A uncertainty of 0.025 ppm

articleTitle: Density Measurement of Thin-Film by Pressure-of-Flotation Method
abstract: Measurements on density differences of silicon crystals by pressure-of-flotation method (PFM) are presented. Temperature stability of the PFM apparatus is being unproved so that more accurate measurement is realized. The PFM is applied for the first time to measure density and thickness of surface layer on silicon crystals

articleTitle: Micropotentiometers with New Disc Resistors and Planar Multijunction Thermal Converters Calibrating High Input Impedance mV-Amplifier
abstract: In the new design of micropotentiometers (upots) planar multijunction thermal converters (PMJTCs) are used together with a new design of the housing and new disc resistors. Only two upots are needed for the step-down chain from 100 mV to 2 mV. A new mV-amplifier in conjunction with a PMJTC is designed to measure the output voltage of the upots. Its high input impedance of >1 MOmega par <10 pF avoids the loading of the output resistor of the upots. Uncertainties in the mV-ac-dc transfer are reduced considerably

articleTitle: Absolute Quantum Efficiency Measurements by Means of Conditioned Polarization Rotation
abstract: The authors propose a new scheme for measuring the quantum efficiency of photon counting detectors by using correlated photons. The scheme consists in measuring the polarization state of one member of a correlated pair after a 90deg polarization rotation conditioned to the detection of the other correlated photon after polarization selection. The authors present experimental results obtained with this scheme compared with traditional correlated photon calibration

articleTitle: Transportable Ac-Dc Transfer Srandard Based on Fast-Reversed Dc
abstract: A compact ac-dc transfer standard system has been developed at AIST. The system is able to perform both ac-dc difference measurements and fast-reversed dc (FRDC) measurements, at voltages from 1V to 10 V. A remote-calibration capability is realized using a digital-output thermal converter as a travelling standard. The system has the capability of calibrating ac-dc transfer instruments with an uncertainty at a 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> level, and thus can be used as a primary ac-dc transfer standard in calibration laboratories

articleTitle: The Mark II Version of the BIPM Torsion-Strip Balance for the Measurement of G
abstract: The BIPM torsion-strip balance used to produce a value for G published in 2001 has been modified with a view to reducing the uncertainty from the 2001 value of about 40 ppm down to about 10 ppm. The poster will not contain a new value for G

articleTitle: Development of compact laser cooled atomic frequency standards
abstract: Two projects of compact cold atom clocks are currently developed: a clock with atoms directly cooled in the microwave cavity and a clock based on coherent population trapping. For each device, different interrogation and detection schemes are evaluated and reported

articleTitle: General-Purpose Current Loop Circuit for Impedance Transducers
abstract: This paper represents the advanced modification of conventional Anderson current loop circuit for impedance transducers (Anderson, 1992). Alongside with well-known features of Anderson loop for pure resistance sensors, the modified version has some additional advantages such as possibility to operate with any type of resistance or reactance sensors, measuring with utmost high accuracy at the expense of optimal digital processing of taken signals

articleTitle: 1 A and 120 mA Thin-Film Multijunction Thermal Converters
abstract: The authors report on the development of thin-film multijunction thermal converters for the measurement of ac current. The materials and designs chosen for these devices have been optimized to provide high accuracy over a wide range of input levels and frequencies. The design details of the MJTCs is presented, and their performance described

articleTitle: Extend AC Voltage Standard to mV Level at 1kHz to 1MHz with Inductive Voltage Dividers
abstract: This paper introduces the work to establish AC voltage standard at mV level at frequency 1kHz, 20kHz, 100kHz and 1 MHz using inductive voltage dividers (IVDs) as the ratio references at NIM. Methods to determine the ratio errors of IVDs, to evaluate the voltage dependence of IVDs and to measure the loading effect are described in this paper

articleTitle: Spectral Line Narrowing in Coupled VCSE-Laser Oscillators for Photonic Microwave Generation
abstract: A novel technique is presented of narrowing the spectral line width of microwave signals generated by heterodyning pairs of VCSELs which form an extended optically coupled cavity. The authors experimentally demonstrate a line width reduction by as much as a factor of 10<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> - to less than 10 kHz

articleTitle: An Improved time domain method for the evaluation of antenna factors of Log-periodic antennas
abstract: We propose a new method for evaluating the free-space antenna factor of a log periodic broadband antenna. The method is based on the techniques of time domain analysis and pulse compression technology. The introduced function enables us to isolate the direct wave from the reflected waves on the ground plane in an open area test site for free-space antenna factor evaluation

articleTitle: A Suspended Laser Interferometer Determination of the Newtonian Constant of Gravitation
abstract: We are completing an experiment to measure the Newtonian constant of gravitation, G, with a suspended Fabry-Perot laser interferometer. The apparatus is operational and systematic errors have been found and eliminated. A result for G is hoped for in summer 2004 with an accuracy of roughly 30 ppm

articleTitle: Collision Shift in Methane
abstract: In this paper, the investigations at the 6-5, 7-6 and 8-7 transition of resolved hyperfine structure of the F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2) </sup>P(7)v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> methane line with the use of a He-Ne laser with a telescopic intracavity light beam expander at a wavelength of 3.39 mum was performed. The light beam diameter in the absorbing methane cell was of about 24 cm. The absorbing cell 8.5 m in length was placed into a permalloy jacket to eliminate the influence of the magnetic field. A second similar telescopic laser all parameters of which were kept constant was used as a frequency reference. In this case, the error of frequency measurements did not exceed 1 Hz, which corresponds in relative units to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>

articleTitle: Molecular Transitions as Medium-Precision Wavelength Standards for Optical Communication
abstract: Molecular vibration-rotation transitions in overtone or combination bands are well suited for providing absolute wavelength standards throughout the wavelength range used for optical communication. In this paper we describe two different implementations of such standards

articleTitle: Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard as a Stable Reference Source of High Current Capability
abstract: The programmable Josephson voltage standard combined with additional variable current source is proposed to be used as an ideal reference source. A stable reference source with sufficient current capability is required for low resistance ratio measurement, for example. Owing to the large Shapiro step of the PJVS array, a simple current source easily available with medium stability is sufficient for this purpose. Experimental result will also be presented to support the proposed idea

articleTitle: The Time and Frequency Domain Measurements of the Magnetic Fields Emitted by Video Display Terminals
abstract: This paper presents the results of measurements of the magnetic fields generated by video display terminals (VDT). For a complete field characterization the time and frequency domain measurements of the field are made at some distances from the screen. There were performed comparative measurements by using a few sensors

articleTitle: Thermodynamical Simulation of the Bolometric Mount. Question on the "Classical Formula of Efficiency" in a Microcalorimeter
abstract: The bolometer mounts classical formula of efficiency is reviewed. By using both a thermodynamical simulation and an analytical approach, it is shown this formula needs a corrective factor for introducing the effect of the thermopile position on the efficiency. The final results present the corrective factor as a function of the thermopile position

articleTitle: Absolute Frequency Measurement and Comparison of UME and BIPM He-Ne/I2 Lasers
abstract: An international comparison of the UME and BIPM He-Ne/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> lasers was carried out. The frequency difference between the lasers was determined by the matrix method. Furthermore, the absolute frequency of the f-component for the UME laser was measured with the BIPM femtosecond laser comb to be (473 612 353 602.0 plusmn 2.2) kHz

articleTitle: Developing Axisymmetric Parametric Model for Electrostatic Force Balance
abstract: An axisymmetric parametric model, based on a 2-dimensional finite element method (FEM), was developed in order to calculate both electric field around a charged coaxial cylindrical capacitor and force between its electrodes. It enables us to optimize design and structure of an electrostatic force balance. This model will be used as a crosscheck by comparing the force derived from its deadweight with the calculated one, especially in the range of from micro-Newton to nano-Newton

articleTitle: Phase Analysis of Coaxial Short and Open
abstract: The phase characteristics of coaxial short and open are analyzed by using the transmission line theory and mode-matching method based on the cosine/sine-Fourier transform. Calculated phase of short and open are compared with one predicted from the data provided by manufacturer

articleTitle: Pumping Single Electrons Through a Laterally Defined Quantum Dot using Surface Acoustic Waves
abstract: We present a new realization of quantized charge pumping operating at 3 GHz. Surface acoustic waves on a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure are used to pump electrons through a quantum dot defined by metallic split gates. The current quantization is determined by the electronic states of the dot

articleTitle: A frequency doubled amplified-fiber laser for molecular iodine spectroscopy near 515 nm
abstract: We have developed a source of 515 nm light by frequency doubling the amplified ouput of an ytterbium-doped fiber laser with a periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) crystal. We present here the main characteristics of the laser and the frequency doubling system, permitting to obtain 22 mW of green radiation in single pass
