articleTitle: 2004 Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Josephson junction devices; laser femtosecond combs; impedance measurement; watt balance; DC voltage measurement; RF free field measurement; AC power measurement; capacitance measurement; time and frequency measurement; inductance measurement; Avogadro constant determination; optical frequency standards using trapped ions/atoms; RF guided wave measurement; cryogenic current comparators; and measurement standards

articleTitle: Precise Calibration System for DC Vector Magnetometers and Approach to its Accrediting
abstract: The automatic calibration system for 3-component vector DC magnetometers of Nurmijarvi Geophysical Observatory (Finland) is in operation for more than 10 years. It is based on a three axes reference coil system and Observatory reference magnetometer. It is shown experimentally that the system allows determining of magnetometer transformation factor with an error below 0.02% and angle errors (non-orthogonality of the magnetometer axes and angles between mechanical and magnetic axes) with error below 1 arc minute. During this period the parameters of the system were measured routinely with absolute measure. In the paper the infrastructure of the system is described and also the procedure of its accrediting is proposed

articleTitle: Optimizing the Series Connection of Thermal Converters for AC-DC Current Calibration - Experimental Verification
abstract: Connecting thermal current converters (TCC) in series for calibration of current ac-dc difference, attention has to be paid to the various current leakages that may occur. Calculations indicate leakage error less than 2*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at frequencies up to 100 kHz. Measured values show that error contributions are less than 1*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at 100 kHz, which is well below the predicted value

articleTitle: A Four-Terminal Pair Coaxial Ratio Bridge for the Realisation of the Capacitance Scale at CSIR-NML.
abstract: A four-terminal coaxial ratio bridge has been constructed at CSIR-NML, South Africa. We present the details of the construction of the bridge and discuss the preliminary results obtained with the bridge

articleTitle: Bilateral Comparisons of the Dissipation Factor of Capacitors at 1 KHZ
abstract: Several attempts have been made to determine the dissipation factor or loss angle tangent of capacitors in the capacitance range from 10 pF to 1 nF and frequencies in the kHz range. In the past these determinations were in agreement, however, the uncertainties were quite high. The new comparisons reported here with considerably reduced uncertainties revealed some problems, the agreements are now within the estimated uncertainties

articleTitle: Establishment of Capacitance Traceability Based on QHR at CMS
abstract: A measurement system for capacitance traceability based on quantized Hall resistance (QHR) has been established at Center for Measurement Standards (CMS), Taiwan. The system comprises an ac-dc calculable resistor, an ac resistance bridge, a capacitance bridge, and a multi-frequency quadrature bridge. By using the multi-frequency quadrature bridge, the capacitance standards can be precisely determined at frequencies from 500 Hz to 5 kHz

articleTitle: Bilateral Comparison of 50 μF Capacitance and its Losses at 50 Hz
abstract: The aim of the project was to compare the calibration capabilities for high valued capacitance (50 μF) and its losses at MIKES-HUT (Finland) and SP (Sweden). Comparison measurements were performed using 50 Hz alternating voltage of 10 V and 200 V. The results show that either capacitance bridge with lead compensation, or a voltage/current sampling system can be used for accurate determination of capacitance value and its loss angle in the microfarad range

articleTitle: Fast Synchronous Ac-Dc-Transfer with Thermal Converters
abstract: The most accurate measurements of the rms (root mean square) values of ac (alternating current) voltages are performed by means of thermal converters (TC) (Klonz, 2002) and digital sampling procedures (Ihlenfeld, 2001 and Ihlenfeld, et. al., 2003) (at low frequencies) with uncertainties of the order of some fractions of muV/V. The main drawback of using TCs relies on the long measuring times required, of a few minutes in most cases. In the following, a simple method for reducing the measuring time and to substantially speed up ac-dc transfer measurements will be described and documented with results of a comparison measurement

articleTitle: A Current Comparator-Based System for Calibration of AC Shunts at Frequencies Up to Audio Frequencies
abstract: An overview of the development of a system comprising of instruments based on the current-comparator technology, for calibration of ac shunts up to audio frequencies is presented. The instruments include an audio-frequency current-comparator, a calculable ac/dc resistor and an ampere-turn balancing circuit. The current comparator is a special multiple ratio audio-frequency current-comparator

articleTitle: Error Analysis of Energy Absorption based NMR-Magnetometer
abstract: The uncertainty of magnetic fields measurement by means of NMR magnetometer has proved to be considerably larger than expected from the magnetometer specifications. Possible error sources have been analysed using a PC-aided marginal oscillator providing a resolution of less than 0.1 muT

articleTitle: Intercomparison of Precision Current Sources in the Range From 10 fA to 10 pA Between PTB and VNIIM
abstract: An intercomparison of precision current sources was carried out for currents between 10 fA to 10 pA. The current sources of both PTB and VNIIM were based on the principle of charging a capacitor using a linear voltage ramp (Rozhdestvenskaya et al., 1979) and (Willenberg et al., 2003). The relative deviation for the values of the sources were found to be between 2.8middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> and 3.1middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, depending on the current range

articleTitle: The NIST Electronic Realization of the Kilogram Project
abstract: The electronic realization of the kilogram project using the new NIST watt balance has been fully operational on a daily basis for several months. Short-term noise is at an all time low with overnight runs exhibiting standard deviations of parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. With the exception of the mass standard, each standard reference has been calibrated with an uncertainty below a part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. Recent improvements that have led to the enhanced performance and current results are discussed

articleTitle: Applications of Microsystems in precision measurements
abstract: Summary form only given. Micro electro mechanical system (MEMS) is a new potential technology to fabricate DC and AC voltage references, AC/DC converters, and high frequency power sensors. In addition, MEMS is very suitable technology for stable reference oscillators. The stability of the components is based on single crystal silicon springs, stress free substrate material (SOI) and metallized surfaces on both capacitor surfaces defining the geometry. The system is either vacuum encapsulated or in protective atmosphere depending on the application. AC and DC voltage references are based on the pull-in voltage, which characterizes a moving plate capacitive MEMS component. An AC/DC converter and a high frequency power sensor utilizes a seesaw structure, which is kept in balance by force feedback. The force is directly proportional to the RMS value of the AC and DC signals. We have also studied the work functions of different metals on silicon to improve the sensor long-term stability. In this paper our new silicon on insulator (SOI) manufacturing process, specially developed for electrical references, will be described. In addition, our recent results will be discussed. The stability and resolution of these new references are compared to existing components such as Zener diodes, thermocouples and rf diodes

articleTitle: Multivalue High Voltage Loss Angle Standard
abstract: The standard of the loss angle tangent (D) is intended for calibration of capacitance bridges at the voltage 1-10 kV and frequency 50 Hz. A high repeatability of the D values is obtained due to special design, and the usage of small-size ceramic capacitors makes the standard portable. The expanded uncertainty of the output parameters of the standard is (1-2)middot10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>+0,001D for the loss angle tangent and 0,1 % (k=2) for the capacitance

articleTitle: A Method to Calculate Antenna Factor by a Single Site Attenuation
abstract: A method to calculate antenna factors with an arbitrary balun and matching circuit by a single site attenuation measurement is proposed. Since explicit evaluation of the field strength is not necessary for this method, it is useful for evaluating antenna factors above the ground plane and so on

articleTitle: Cold Atom Absolute Gravimeter for the Watt Balance
abstract: We are building a cold atom absolute gravimeter based on atom interferometry with a projected accuracy of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> g. It is part of the French watt balance project intending to link the SI Kg unit to fundamental constants

articleTitle: On strategies for automatic bridge balancing
abstract: Automatic balancing of coaxial ac impedance bridges ask for simple, robust and fast strategies which can be easily implemented on PC controllers. A general approach toward balancing bridge networks (with several injection and detection points) based on secant's method and its generalizations is here proposed. Experimental results on a test circuit are given

articleTitle: Microwave Free Space Calibration Methods
abstract: Different methods for the calibration of a free space measurement system are presented. The free space system can be used for the measurement of the permittivity or permeability of planar material probes. Due to systematic errors a calibration of the measurement setup is necessary. For a high accuracy it is advantageous to use calibration methods where the calibration standards are all of equal mechanical lengths. The theory and the implementation of the extended LNN and LRR procedures in a free space system are therefore presented

articleTitle: Calculable Filter for Josephson Arbitrary Wafeform Synthesis
abstract: Calculable AC source can be built of Josephson arrays driven by properly modulated excitation pulse stream. When Sigma-Delta modulation is used excessive high frequency noise is produced which has to be filtered out without compromising low frequency output signal. An adequate filter for this purpose was developed within a Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesizer (JAWS) project (Chevtchenko, et.al., 2004)

articleTitle: New Direct Current Sensor Based on Magnetic Potential Self-Balance and Feedback Compensation
abstract: A new type of direct current sensor is developed which includes two parts: magnetic potential self-balance circuit and feedback compensation circuit. The characteristics of the device are: simple construction, good stability and reliability, and high precision (the error less than 0.1% in range of 40%~100% rated current)

articleTitle: Secure Control of Instruments via the Internet
abstract: A system for secure, remote operation of instruments using the Internet as a transport network for control signals and measurement data is presented. The system allows persons at different locations to control each other's electrical instruments regardless of firewalls and network address translators. A viable application is Internet-enabled calibration

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Femtosecond Optical Frequency Combs at NPL
abstract: A second femtosecond optical frequency comb has been implemented at NPL. This higher repetition rate system offers several advantages over our existing comb, and enables the accuracy of the frequency measurement process to be tested. Results of absolute frequency measurements carried out using the two different systems are compared

articleTitle: Wavelet-Based Method for Tracking Flicker Level
abstract: A shift-invariant wavelet-based method is developed to detect the envelope of voltage flickers. It uses a linear phase complex wavelet and the quadrature signal approach in wavelet-domain, and takes a fast dyadic pyramid algorithm not a time consuming shift -invariant one. Just two smoothed wavelet transforms and one detailed wavelet transform are implemented. These make the method fast and accurate

articleTitle: Sinis Josephson Junction Series Arrays for Operation in the Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesiser
abstract: The Josephson arbitrary waveform synthesiser (JAWS) is based on Josephson junctions operated by short pulses. We describe the development of SINIS Josephson series arrays for applications in the JAWS that were performed within the framework of the EU-funded JAWS project

articleTitle: NIST Service for Measuring the Step Response of High-Speed Samplers and the Output of High-Speed Pulse Generators
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) provides a service for measuring parameters associated with the step response of high-speed (transition durations ges 5 ps) samplers and the signals output by high-speed pulse generators. These parameters include transition duration (rise time and/or fall time), waveform amplitude, overshoot, and undershoot

articleTitle: Determination of the AC-DC Voltage Transfer Difference of High Voltage Transfer Standards at Low Frequencies
abstract: The ac-dc transfer difference at low frequencies of thermal converters for higher voltages with planar multijunction thermal converters (PMJTCs) and series resistors has been determined by using only the established linear change of the low-frequency ac-dc current transfer difference of the PMJTC with input power. Uncertainties of less than 1 muV/V are achieved up to 1000V

articleTitle: Uncertainties in the Measurement of Power Harmonics and Flicker
abstract: Uncertainties of a precision measurement system developed at NML for traceable calibration of three-phase instruments measuring harmonics of current up to 20 A, voltage fluctuation and flicker are discussed. The analysis shows that current and voltage harmonics up to the 99th and fluctuating voltages can be generated and measured with relative uncertainties close to 1times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>

articleTitle: Self-consistent uncertainty calculations in voltage and resistance metrology
abstract: Least-squares optimisation using Lagrange multipliers is used to determine self-consistent values of the parameters that enter into calibration of a voltage source using a Josephson voltage standard including those of the measurement system itself

articleTitle: Cooper pair sluice: A fast and accurate single-island charge pump
abstract: We have carried out first measurements on a novel type of a charge pump nicknamed the Cooper pair "sluice". The device is an adiabatic flux-assisted Cooper pair pump consisting of a mesoscopic superconducting island and of two SQUID loops. The operation is based on the periodic manipulation of a single voltage gate and two input coils controlling the magnetic flux through the SQUID loops. Based on theoretical estimates the device is capable of producing as high as 0.1 nA currents at better than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> accuracy and looks thus like a promising candidate for the current source in completing the quantum measurement triangle. In spite of several nonidealities in our preliminary measurement setup, we have succeeded in verifying the pumping behavior of the sluice. The pumped currents were quite high, several hundred pA, but the accuracy needs to be increased. The results obtained so far suggest various ways of improving the measurement setup

articleTitle: DC-Current Source controlled by NMR
abstract: For the calibration of magnetic instruments a DC current source controlled by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) has been developed for currents in the range from 0.3 to 1 A. Depending on the absorption line-width of the NMR sample a resolution of less than 1 muA and a current instability of less than 1 ppm over 8 hours can be achieved

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Power Calibrations using Power Splitters
abstract: A new RF and microwave power calibration system using power splitters has been developed and implemented. A novel method to derive the calibration factor from the scattering parameters of the power splitter and reflection coefficients of reference sensor and sensor under test has been presented. This approach proved to be more efficient

articleTitle: Digital Compensation Unit for Impedance Metrology
abstract: A two-channel compensation unit based on an application of a digital signal processor is described. This special device, having implemented the algorithm of the synchronous filtering, is used for the compensations of spurious voltages in the measurement set-up of the three-voltmeter method. The unit works in frequency range of 500 Hz-5 kHz. If the compensation unit is applied into the system, it has attained the level of residual spurious voltages about a few muVs. Thanks to this fact, the calibration of inductance standards in range 1mH-100mH can be made with the uncertainty less than 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4 </sup>

articleTitle: Reduced Uncertainty of Measurement for Vector Network Analysers Employing Regression During Calibration
abstract: We formulate the calibration process for a one-port vector network analyser (VNA) as a regression problem making full use of the uncertainty information available for the indicated and 'true' voltage reflection coefficients (VRCs) of the standards. The benefit of over-determining the calibration in terms or reduced uncertainties is demonstrated for VRC measurements at RF frequencies

articleTitle: DDS Based NMR Magnetometer in Slovenian Calibration Laboratory
abstract: Presented absorption type proton magnetometer uses direct digital synthesizer and DSP instead of marginal oscillator, therefore frequency measurement uncertainty is negligible. Frequency modulation of high frequency signal is used instead of magnetic field modulation. With the magnetometer described and the existent permanent magnet the accreditation range of the LMM could be extended.

articleTitle: Euromet 495 Comparison of High Direct Voltage Measurements up to 100 kV
abstract: The results are described of an international comparison of measurement techniques at direct voltages up to 100 kV. (EUROMET Project 495)

articleTitle: Frequency Measurement of the Iodine-Stabilized Ar+ Laser at 501 nm
abstract: We report the first absolute frequency measurement of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">127 </sup>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> hyperfine components of the R(26)62-0 transition at 501.7 nm with an optical clockwork based on a femtosecond laser frequency comb generator

articleTitle: Absolute Frequency Measurements of 1.5 Micron Acetylene-Stabilized Lasers
abstract: A pair of 1.5 mum diode laser frequency standards stabilized to <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> have been developed at NPL. Their stability and long-term reproducibility have been characterized, and the absolute frequencies of several acetylene lines measured using a combination of frequency chain, femtosecond comb and passive optical frequency comb technologies

articleTitle: Linking Microwave Remote-Sensing Measurements to Fundamental Noise Standards
abstract: We outline the formalism for linking microwave remote-sensing measurements to fundamental noise standards and estimate the achievable uncertainty. Plans for the development and use of standard radiometers for this purpose ar presented

articleTitle: Updated Calibration Method for Coaxial Microcalorimeters
abstract: A key point in the realization of power standards with the microcalorimeter technique is the determination of the microcalorimeter losses and of their influence upon the measurand, i.e. the effective efficiency of the sensor used as thermal load. At IEN Galileo Ferraris, a simple procedure has been experienced that makes the microcalorimeter constant determination easier. Experiments done with a coaxial microcalorimeter in 50 MHz-18 GHz range have shown a significant accuracy improvement for the Italian national power standard

articleTitle: S-Parameter Measurement Comparison Euromet.EM.RF-S16: Data Analysis
abstract: We report about the data analysis of this first formal scattering parameter comparison of the coaxial 2.4mm system. Multivariate statistics and a Monte Carlo method are applied to determine a comparison reference value (CRV) with a 95% confidence region

articleTitle: Progress on the NPL Watt Balance: Alignment and Measurements
abstract: After modifications to the balance support structure, the apparatus was run for a short time in July 2003 and showed agreement with the data presented at CPEM 2002 within existing alignment limitations. The balance is presently being modified to allow accurate alignment of the coil in vacuum and further measurements are carried out in 2004 with the aim of determining the alignment uncertainties and producing a value for Planck's constant

articleTitle: A Two-Stage, Guarded Inductive Voltage Divider for Use in Coaxial Bridges Employed in the Derivation of Capacitance Unit From Quantized Hall Resistance
abstract: The traceability chain to derive the capacitance unit from the quantized Hall resistance (QHR) comprises a few coaxial bridges. These bridges use a main two-stage, guarded inductive voltage divider (IVD) to provide the voltage ratio. The design details and calibration results of the IVD constructed partly at INMETRO and partly at PTB, with technical support from PTB and CENAM, are presented

articleTitle: Corrosion Detection and Thickness Evaluation Utilizing Active Near-Field Microwave Nondestructive Testing Techniques
abstract: An inventive method utilizing microwave nondestructive testing techniques for enhanced detection and evaluation of rust under paint has been developed. The results are promising and show that the use of a layer of dielectric material with known properties to replace the standoff layer (air) yields significant improvements in the measurement sensitivity and resolution

articleTitle: Preliminary Experiment of Comparison Between a 1-V NbN-Based Programmable and a Conventional Josephson Array
abstract: We tried a direct comparison between a 1-V NbN-based programmable superconductor-normal metal-superconductor (SNS) Josephson array and a conventional superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) Josephson array. In preliminary experiment the voltage difference of the two arrays was -4.3 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> V in average of 10 measurement sets. The deviation is resulted from the fluctuations of the background in the measurement set

articleTitle: An Automated System for the Precision Calibration of High Value Resistance Standards using a Novel Scanner
abstract: A fully automated system for the precision calibration of high value resistance standards of 100 MOmega, and greater has been built and is in use at NML Australia. The precision obtained is due to the use of a novel scanner for the selection of reference and unknown resistance standards, the temperature control of these, and the characterisation of the comparator used, a commercially available teraohmmeter

articleTitle: Superconductive Reactive Components for Metrological Applications
abstract: Superconductive reactive components seem to be very appealing for many metrological applications. Some preliminary tests have proved the possibility of building inductors with quality factor higher than some thousands in the acoustic frequency band, but have also arisen some problems for which further investigations are necessary

articleTitle: Long-Distance Optical Link to Primary Standard and Absolute Frequency Measurement in the 28-THZ Spectral Region
abstract: We developed a stabilized frequency distribution system to transfer a reference through a 43 km standard telecommunication fiber optic. This low noise link has been used to perform frequency comparisons between LPL and SYRTE clocks

articleTitle: Measurement of Berry's Phase using a Time-Domain Atom Interferometer
abstract: We propose a novel method of the measurement of Berry's phase free from the dynamical phase shift for partial cycles of rotating magnetic field in parameter space by using a time-domain atom interferometer. The experimental results are presented and discussed

articleTitle: NRC-METAS-PTB Collaboration Part 3: Frequency, Current and Field Dependence in the Quantized Hall and Longitudinal Ac Resistance
abstract: To improve the consistency of AC quantized Hall resistance (QHR) measurements, the NRC, PTB and METAS have formed a collaboration. A study of the influences of the measurement apparatus on the AC QHR measurement results was presented. Preliminary results of the shape of plateau i = 2, measured at different laboratories, as well as the effect of the back-gate on the plateaus measured on a PTB sample are presented

articleTitle: A Simple Method for Fabricating Silicon Single Electron Devices for Metrology Applications
abstract: A simple method, based on overlapping the dosage distribution of the discretely electron beam written nano-dots, was employed to fabricate silicon single electron transistor. The electronic characteristics of fabricated Si-based SET were analyzed, and found to be consistent with the expected behavior of electron transport through a gated quantum dot.

articleTitle: Indirect method observing QHR steps at 900kHz
abstract: Differential resistances of QHR were measured with increasing magnetic field from zero to 14T at 0.3K by dual frequency current combinations of 10kHz and 10.0001 kHz, 10kHz and 100.0001kHz, 900kHz and 900.0001kHz. A few thousands data of 0.1 Hz voltages were added by Excel software and then the QHR steps constructed again. One of the two samples were tested and got sharp steps at 900kHz as measured by a DC current, but the other one showed not so good shape. Therefore, it is easy method to check QHR's characteristics for high frequency region

articleTitle: A Preliminary Measurement of h/mRb using Ultracold Atoms
abstract: We use Bloch oscillations in a horizontal and a vertical moving standing wave to transfer a large number of photon recoils to atoms. By measuring the photon recoil of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb using velocity selective Raman transitions to select a subrecoil velocity class and to measure the final accelerated velocity class, we have determined h/m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Rb</sub> with a relative precision of 0.4 ppm

articleTitle: Time transfer using GPS carrier phase measurements by self-developed KRISS software
abstract: We report on test results of precision time transfer using GPS carrier phase by self-developed processing software. Carrier phase measurements using the Ashtech Z12-T receivers over baselines ranging from zero to several thousands of kilometers were carried out for evaluating the performance of time transfer. We used the self-developed processing software in this time transfer experiment

articleTitle: Systematic Errors in Noise Parameter Determination Due to Imperfect Source Impedance Measurement
abstract: The paper presents a rigorous analysis of systematic errors in the four-noise parameter determination of a two-port network using the cold-source technique. The method is based on an original model that accounts for imperfectly-measured source reflection coefficients due to residual errors within a vector network analyzer (VNA). The authors show that even small VNA errors may seriously deteriorate the accuracy of the noise parameters when characterizing low-noise pseudomorphic high-electron mobility transistors (PHEMTs)

articleTitle: NRC Quantum Hall Devices for National Measurement Institutes
abstract: At CPEM'02 in Ottawa the NRC Electrical Standards Group undertook to fabricate a batch of Hall devices suitable for use at National Measurement Institutes as resistance standards. One wafer has been fabricated to date and testing of the electrical parameters of devices has commenced. The paper described the fabrication parameters, and preliminary test results

articleTitle: Extending the Range and Utility of Femtosecond Combs
abstract: To extend the range of utility of femtosecond comb technology at NPL, two comb systems are being built: a transportable system, to enable measurements to be made at locations other than our own laboratory; and a Cr:forsterite laser-based comb, to extend the spectral range to cover the telecommunications bands

articleTitle: Ultimate Speed of Dissipative Pumping of Cooper Pairs
abstract: Ultimate speed of operation of a 3-junction superconducting cooper pair pump with local resistors (R-pump) is estimated. It is shown that due to essential damping of Josephson coupling accurate pumping is possible at relatively high frequencies as compared to the single electron pumps

articleTitle: Iodine Frequency Stabilized Lasers in CMI
abstract: The paper describes recent development and improvement of optical frequency standards used in CMI for length metrology - iodine stabilized lasers 543nm and 532nm. The iodine cells, experimental set-up, operating parameters and results of comparisons are summarized together with absolute frequency measurements of these lasers and 633nm standard.

articleTitle: First Experience with the Commercial Quantum Hall Resistance Standard at the Czech Metrological Institute
abstract: Commercial quantum Hall resistance standard has been put into operation at the CMI. Small, but systematic discrepancy between results obtained at 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> and 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> QHE plateaux was observed and its possible origin will be discussed. Unpredictable drift of the built-in 100Omega transfer standard will also be dealt with

articleTitle: Ramped Capacitor Current Source with Software Controlled Non-Linearity Compensation
abstract: A high accuracy ramped capacitor current source has been developed with software controlled compensation for the voltage ramp non-linearity. Within several seconds, a voltage ramp within typically 10 ppm of any desired value between a few mV/s and several hundreds of mV/s can be reached. Using a high quality air capacitor, high accuracy currents below 10 pA can be generated

articleTitle: Antenna Radiation Pattern Measurement at a Reduced Distance
abstract: A method has been developed to obtain the far-field radiation pattern of an antenna at a reduced distance where the far-field distance condition is not satisfied. It uses an asymptotic antenna transmission formula and angular mode deconvolution technique to determine the far-field radiation pattern

articleTitle: Frequency Measurements of 778 nm Rubidium Two Photon Diode Laser Standards
abstract: A pair of 778 nm rubidium two photon diode laser frequency standards has been developed at NPL. Their systematic sensitivity to various experimental parameters has been investigated and their stability and reproducibility characterized. Absolute frequency measurements have been made for two hyperfine components

articleTitle: Calculation of the Magnetic Field of a Cryogenic Current Comparator
abstract: An analytic expression for the magnetic field of the filaments surrounded by the toroidal superconducting shield has been derived. This will be used for the derivation of the error expression for the cryogenic current comparator (CCC)

articleTitle: Present Status of the a Vogadro Constant Determination from Silicon Crystals with Natural Isotopic Composition
abstract: The determination of the Avogadro constant from two selected silicon crystals is described. The density, molar mass, and lattice spacing of the two crystals were measured at NMU, PTB, IRMM, IMGC, and NIST. When all the data are combined, it leads to the Avogadro constant of 6.022 1353 (21) times 1023 mol<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> with a relative combined standard uncertainty of 3.4 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>

articleTitle: Quasi-Monolithic Toroidal Cross Capacitor
abstract: A quasi-monolithic 0.5 pF toroidal cross capacitor has been developed that can be used as a standard to determine frequency dependence of a Thompson-Lampard calculable capacitor (TLCC), and for direct comparison of the TLCCs and for a primary standard of loss angle and a maintenance standard of capacitance. The instability of capacitance is expected to be not exceed 5X10"8 per year

articleTitle: With an Intense Bismuth ION Beam Toward Accumulation of a Weighable Mass ofAtoms
abstract: An experiment for the direct measurement of the atomic mass unit was proposed (Glaser, 1991). To obtain a weighable mass a dedicated set-up for the low energy beam transport (LEBT) of heavy ions is needed. The type of the ion source used as well as measurements of the extracted bismuth ion beam is presented. The LEBT-section is discussed using SIMION-3D calculations

articleTitle: Contact Resistance of PL173 Quantum Hall Samples Developed in Euromet Project N°346
abstract: The authors have measured the physical and metrological parameters of QHE samples developed by BNM-LNE and LEP in Euromet project 346. It appears that the samples marked PL173 have good characteristics, but suffer from a contact resistance that behaves asymmetric with respect to the current polarity. At the point where electrons are injected into the two-dimensional electron gas, the increase in contact resistance occurs at significantly lower currents than for currents in the other direction. Several methods have been tried to improve the behaviour of the contacts, but so far without success

articleTitle: A Consideration of Linearity in Heterodyne Detection
abstract: Linearity of heterodyne detection is important in intermediate frequency(IF) substitution method for radio frequency(RF) attenuation measurement. Basically, the conversion equation V=kappaE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">alpha</sup> (alpha=1, kappa=constant) is valid in a proper range of E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> where E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> and V are RF input and IF output amplitudes, respectively. This paper discusses the possibility that alphane1

articleTitle: Optical frequency measurements with laser cooled Sr atoms
abstract: This paper reports the frequency measurement with an accuracy in the 100 kHz range of several optical transitions of atomic Sr. Measurements are performed with a frequency chain based on a femto-second laser and referenced to a hydrogen maser. They allowed the determination with a 70 kHz uncertainty of the energy of the 5s5p <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3 </sup>Po state and the direct observation and frequency measurement of the doubly forbidden <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> rarr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> transition at 698 nm. This line has a natural width of 10 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> Hz and can be used for a new generation of optical frequency standards using atoms trapped in a light shift free dipole trap

articleTitle: Progress in Coupled Microwave Resonators for Sensitive Bolometric Detection
abstract: We report further development of a novel form of bolometric detector which may have widespread application to particle detection and energy resolved measurement, applicable to massive particles, photons or even phonons

articleTitle: Reference System for Traceable Calibration of High Current Frequency Response
abstract: Two different reference systems for calibration of frequency response for high current measuring equipment are tested. A system based on a conventional current transformer fitted with a low current shunt and a sampling voltmeter is shown to have acceptable accuracy in whole of the frequency range investigated

articleTitle: In-Service Characterization of Electronic Voltage Standards
abstract: We have investigated the feasibility of measuring the pressure and humidity dependences of electronic voltage standards (EVSs) by analysis of data from routine within-group comparisons of a group standard. Some of the standards were found to have significant sensitivity to either pressure or humidity

articleTitle: Cavity Pulling Shift Measured from AC Zeeman Shift in an Optically Pumped Cs Beam Standard
abstract: The off-resonant component of the RF spectrum causes an AC Zeeman shift in the clock transition frequency. This shift has been measured by detuning an off-resonant sideband of a resonant RF field fed into the Ramsey cavity. This method directly measures the buildup of the frequency-dependent RF power within the cavity. The authors have calculated the detuning slope of the cavity resonance curve at the clock transition frequency. The value of the cavity pulling shift of KRISS-1 has been determined

articleTitle: A Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard Chip using Arrays of NbN/TiN/NbN/TiN/NbN Double-Junction Stacks Operated at 10K
abstract: A programmable Josephson voltage standard chip using arrays of NbN/TiN/NbN/TiN/NbN double-junction stacks was fabricated and operated at 10 K. The circuit with over 260,000 junctions showed constant voltage steps at +/- 6 V when driven at 11 GHz microwave bias. Further investigation is required to achieve 10 V operation at the desired design frequency of 19 GHz

articleTitle: Optical Frequency Measurements and Standards at Near Infrared
abstract: Absolute frequencies of an acetylene-stabilized laser at 1542 nm and an iodine-stabilized Nd:YAG at 1319 nm are measured at their second harmonics by use of a femtosecond optical comb based on a mode-locked Ti:sapphire laser. A frequency measurement system based on a mode-locked fiber laser (1.56mum) is also being developed for metrological applications in the telecommunication bands

articleTitle: Certifying the Degree of Perfection of Silicon Single Crystals for the Avogadro Project by Measuring the Amount of Copper Silicide Precipitated in the Voids
abstract: A procedure has been developed for determining the number of missing atoms in a silicon crystal. Possible voids are filled with Cu <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>Si by indiffusion of copper. After removal of the interstitially dissolved copper, the samples are digested and the copper content is determined by isotope-dilution mass spectrometry. The detection limit of this highly specific and accurate measurement method was developed sufficiently to certify the degree perfection of the silicon single crystals used to enable a redetermination of the Avogadro constant, N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub>, to the required level: lower than 2 times 10 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub> combined standard uncertainty

articleTitle: Measured Permittivity Ratio of Argon/Helium using Cross Capacitors
abstract: In order to improve primary pressure standards at NIST we have measured the dielectric permittivity ratio of argon to helium epsiv <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ar</sub>/epsiv<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">He</sub> using two cross capacitors that were operated side by side in a thermostatted bath (plusmn0.002 K) over a temperature range (273-323) K and over a pressure range (0-6) MPa. For these measurements we have used both an 8-ring toroidal cross capacitor and a 64-rod linear array cross capacitor in pressure chambers separated by a sensitive differential pressure cell

articleTitle: Simulation of Direct Current Sensor Based on Magnetic Potential Self-Balance and Feedback Compensation
abstract: A mathematical model for new direct current sensor based on the magnetic potential self-balance and feedback compensation is developed. Theory for the mathematical model is explained. The simulation results of the system are shown that the accuracy of the dc sensor is better than 0.1%

articleTitle: The Shot Noise Thermometer: Primary Electronic Thermometry using the Noise from a Tunnel Junction
abstract: We present a thermometer based on the electrical noise from a tunnel junction. In this thermometer, temperature is related to voltage across the junction by a relative microwave noise measurement with only the use of the electron charge, Boltzmann's constant, and assumption that electrons in a metal obey Fermi-Dirac statistics (Lafe Spietz, 2003)

articleTitle: Narrow-Line Diode Laser System for the S-D Transmon of Ca+Ion
abstract: An extended-cavity Littman-type diode laser, aiming the linewidth below 1 Hz, is in process to be developed. This laser is planned as the clock laser for the precise spectroscopy of the electric quadrupole 4s2S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">½</sup> - 3d2D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5/2</sup>, transition of a 43Ca+ion.

articleTitle: Mobile Standard of Voltage Scale Transformation Coefficient
abstract: Developed and produced mobile standard of voltage scale transformation coefficient (VSTC) is described below. Mobile standard is intended for transfer of VSTC unit to voltage transformers working standards and precision working voltage transformers on the places of their installation at the frequency 50 Hz for voltage classes 110, 150, 220 and 330 kV

articleTitle: 1000 V DC Voltage Ratio Calibration at VNIIM
abstract: To calibrate dc voltage calibrators and voltmeters above 10 V with ratio uncertainty less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> resistive dividers are used. Method for the calibration of resistive divider at applied voltage up to 1000 V is described. Estimated relative combined uncertainty of 1000 V/10 V was 0.1 ppm (k=2)

articleTitle: Sampling Capabilities of a DMM - Determination of Key Parameters
abstract: A sampling method for indirect measurement of all relevant parameters of sampling device is presented. One can determine sampling frequency inaccuracy, integration interval inaccuracy and latency time. All these parameters can be determined with relative error less than 10 ppm, except latency time whose absolute accuracy is about 60 ns

articleTitle: Performance Testing of Time Comparison using GPS Smoothed P3 Code and IGS Ephemerides
abstract: In this paper, the characteristics of time transfer using GPS smoothed P3 code with IGS precise ephemerides are studied. The carrier-smoothed P3 code is used to compute the timing information and IGS precise ephemerides are adopted to calculate the satellites' coordinates. The two modifications have different effects. The IGS precise ephemerides are more accurate than the broadcast ephemerides; hence, the REFGPS results computing from different satellites are more accurate. On the other hand, since the carrier-smoothed P3 code has smaller noise level than P3 code does, the differences of REFGPS between laboratories are more accurate. The time comparison between laboratories are also processed to show our program is sound and effective

articleTitle: IEN Cs Fountain Primary Frequency Standard: Contribution to the International Atomic Time and Blackbody Shift Measurements
abstract: Since last year, IEN Cs fountain (IEN-CsFI) has started to contribute to the atomic international time (TAI). During this period we have also provided the first direct measurements of the black-body radiation shift for Cs performed with a cold atoms standard. The results suggest a review of this bias evaluation in order to ensure a 10-15 accuracy level for fountains

articleTitle: Proposed Laboratory Tests of Time-Variation of the Fundamental Constants using the Ensemble of Frequency Standards at NPL
abstract: Comparisons between atomic frequency standards can provide stringent experimental limits to the present-day local variation of the fundamental constants. We analyse the potential sensitivity of the constants of the ensemble of standards under development at NPL to such variations. Femtosecond combs provide the enabling technology for the proposed tests

articleTitle: Highly-Accurate Real-Time GPS Carrier Phase Disciplined Oscillator
abstract: A low-cost, highly-accurate and real-time GPS carrier phase disciplined oscillator system based on a single-frequency receiver is presented. By using the atmosphere-free model of the carrier phase with time-series-noise-free, and performing the time-difference, the low-cost oscillator could be automatically steered to obtain the very high frequency accuracy and stability in the short term (1 sec.) as well as in the long term (1 day).

articleTitle: A Method, and its Instrumentation, for Measurement of Small Differences of Vectorial Values
abstract: The paper considers a measurement method that determines small differences of vectorial values (less than 1% in magnitude and 0.02 rad in phase). The solution is based on the use of 2-channel digital instrument for non-coherent sampling of harmonic signal instant values. Method description includes analysis of methodic inaccuracies. The study demonstrates that common off-the-shelf power analyzer is made applicable, due to the method proposed, to onsite calibration of instrument transformers of commercial frequency current or voltage

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Distributed Cavity Phase Shift in an Atomic Fountain Frequency Standard
abstract: The authors have estimated the effect of distributed cavity phase shift using numerical simulation for a microwave power fed by two coaxial cables. The tolerance of the phase difference and the ratio of the amplitude is found to be 10mrad and 0.4 respectively, in order to achieve the uncertainty of 5times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup>

articleTitle: A DC Voltage Reference Based on MEMS
abstract: A micromechanical moving plate capacitor has been designed and fabricated for use as the key component in a DC voltage reference. The reference is based on the characteristic pull-in property of a capacitive MEMS device. New device design and characterization results are presented

articleTitle: Guide to the Conversion of Specified Bounds into Uncertainty
abstract: To calculate type B uncertainty from bounds on manufacturer's specification, two distributions, normal and rectangular, are approximately assumed depending on the setting of thresholds on testing. The crossover threshold bound-width was 2radic3 times one standard deviation of distribution on whole products, which corresponds the yield 90%

articleTitle: Bloch Oscillating Transistor as the Null Detector in the Quantum Metrology Triangle
abstract: The Bloch oscillating transistor is a new mesoscopic current amplifier with estimated white current noise below 1 fA/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> and potentially low 1/f noise. The operation principle and recent results of the BOT are presented and its potential in closing the quantum metrology triangle is analysed

articleTitle: Fundamental Constants - True Values and Expectations
abstract: When evaluating measurements, the distinction between the true values of the physical constants on the one hand and their formally defined statistical expectation on the other should be strictly abided. Otherwise measurement uncertainties might not localise the pertaining true values

articleTitle: A Wavelet Based Method for Locating Bursts of Harmonics
abstract: Harmonic analysers are used to test the fluctuating harmonic emissions of electrical appliances to international regulations. This paper describes a wavelet-based method of measuring level changing harmonics (bursts) for use in the calibration of these analysers. The method is shown to be reliable for measuring various mixtures of harmonics

articleTitle: The Engineering Model of the Space Clock PHARAO
abstract: The construction of an engineering model of the cold atom space clock is drawing to a close. The clock has four main sub-systems: the cesium tube, the command system, the laser and the microwave sources. In this paper we describe their physical package and present the tests of their performances

articleTitle: Direct Resistance Comparisons from the QHR to 100 Megohm using a Cryogemic Current Comparator
abstract: We describe the operation of a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) bridge that attains high current sensitivity while maintaining stability under a range of measurement conditions. Measurements of 100 MCI standard resistors and cryogenic thin-film resistors have been made at low voltage levels, based directly on a quantized Hall resistance (QHR) standard

articleTitle: Effect of lattice strains in the measurement of the (220) lattice spacing of silicon
abstract: The measurement of the Si lattice parameter a<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with an uncertainty lower than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>, requires to study the role of lattice strains of various kind. The Takagi's approach has been used to study the modulation parameters of outgoing X-ray beams

articleTitle: Evaluation of Frequency Behaviour of Coils for Reference Magnetic Field Generation
abstract: The frequency behaviour of coils used for the calibration of magnetic field meters is evaluated starting from the construction parameters (geometrical dimensions, number of turns) by considering an equivalent circuit with lumped parameters and solving the related equation system in the frequency domain. The computed frequency behaviour is validated by comparison with experimental data

articleTitle: A Resilient Backpropagation Neural Network based Phase Correction System for Automatic Digital AC Bridges
abstract: The present paper describes the development of an ANN based phase correction system which has been employed in conjunction with a real automatic digital ac bridge. The proposed ANN-based phase corrector has been developed using backpropagation learning employing resilient backpropagation (popularly known as RPROP). Significant improvements have been obtained in the proposed phase correction system for measuring impedance and reported in the paper

articleTitle: On Possible Use of Quantized Voltages of Shapiro Steps for Absolute Inductance Calibration and Governing Direct Currents
abstract: It is suggested to make use of Shapiro step quantized voltages for controllable changes of magnetic flux in a superconducting loop. This makes it possible to produce a stable direct current (DC) scale by an external DC controller with the current magnitude adjustable in a ramping manner without unlocking the feedback. Also, a mutual inductance inherent to the setup can be calibrated on practically zero frequency in terms of fundamental constants and the second

articleTitle: Determination of DC Voltage Ratio of Self-Calibrating Divider
abstract: This paper presents two techniques to determine the ratios of resistive dc voltage dividers up to 1 kV. The techniques are based on absolute calibration methods. The set-up requires equipment commonly available in most standard laboratory and is capable of providing high accuracy calibration under practical laboratory working conditions
